title: Armenia Economic Activity Growth Slows in June
summary: Armenia’s economic activity rose 7.7% year-on-year in June 2026, slowing from an 11.7% increase in May, which marked the highest growth since December 2025. Growth moderated in industrial production (4.0% vs 9.5% in May) and construction output (25.4% vs 27.1%). In addition, retail sales edged down 0.1%, after being flat in the previous month. Meanwhile, the volume of services except trade continued to rise, climbing 19.7% following a 14.7% increase. On a monthly basis, economic activity increased 4.4%, easing from a 9.9% growth in May. For the first half of the year, overall economic activity was 7.9% higher than in the corresponding period a year earlier.

title: Eurozone Lending Rises Less than Expected
summary: Bank lending to Eurozone households rose 3% year-on-year to €7.22 trillion in June 2026, the same as in the previous month and below market forecasts of 3.1%. Business lending stood at 4.0% in June, unchanged from May. Overall private sector credit, including households and non-financial corporations, rose 3.9%.

title: Hong Kong Imports Growth Surges to 1992 High
summary: Imports to Hong Kong rose 45.5% year-on-year to USD 693 billion in June 2026, following a 42% rise in the previous month. The latest figure marked the largest import growth since February 1992, driven largely by increased purchases in electrical machinery, apparatus, appliances, and electrical parts thereof (+54.2%), telecommunications and sound recording and reproducing apparatus and equipment (+67.3%), and office machines and automatic data processing machines (+53.6%). By source, imports recorded the strongest growth among major suppliers from Korea (+176.7%), Vietnam (+106.8%), India (+95.4%), Malaysia (+62.4%), and Mainland China (+41.0%). For the first half of 2026, imports grew 40.6% compared to the same period a year earlier, lifted by higher inflows of non-ferrous metals (+197.8%), telecommunications and sound recording and reproducing apparatus and equipment (+71.5%), and electrical machinery, apparatus, appliances, and electrical parts thereof (+47.0%).

title: Hong Kong Trade Deficit Narrows in June
summary: Hong Kong's trade deficit narrowed to $52 billion in June 2026 from $58.9 billion in the same month a year earlier. Exports surged 53.4% year-on-year to a four-month high of $641.1 billion, driven mainly by stronger shipments of electrical machinery, apparatus and appliances, and electrical parts thereof (57.2%), and office machines and automatic data processing machines (93.2%). Exports to Asia rose 54.4%, while shipments to other key markets, such as the US (114.3%) and Mexico (94.2%), also increased. Meanwhile, imports climbed 45.4% from a year earlier to a three-month high of $693 billion, supported by higher purchases of electrical machinery, apparatus and appliances, and electrical parts thereof (54.2%) and telecommunications and sound recording and reproducing apparatus and equipment (67.3%). Import growth was particularly strong from Mainland China and Hong Kong (41.0%) and South Korea (176.7%). During the January–June period, the total trade deficit reached $294.6 billion.

title: FX Updates: Norwegian Krone Depreciates by 0.76%
summary: Top currency losers are Norwegian Krone (-0.76%), South Korean Won (-0.72%) and Dollar Index (-0.23%). Gains are led by Indian Rupee (0.48%), Swedish Krona (0.46%), Australian Dollar (0.43%), Euro (0.31%), British Pound (0.23%) and Japanese Yen (0.16%).

title: Hong Kong Exports Reach Record High
summary: Exports from Hong Kong surged 53.4% year-on-year to an all-time high of $641.1 billion in June 2026, accelerating from a 40.8% increase in the previous month. It marked the strongest annual growth since March 1984, driven primarily by robust shipments of electrical machinery, apparatus and appliances, and electrical parts thereof (57.2% vs 56.1% in May), office machines and automatic data processing machines (93.2% vs 50.2%), telecommunications and sound recording and reproducing apparatus and equipment (69.9% vs 37.6%), miscellaneous manufactured articles (58.6% vs 29.6%), power generating machinery and equipment (23.5% vs 7.6%), and professional, scientific and controlling instruments and apparatus (18.1% vs 7.3%). Regionally, exports to Asia climbed 54.4%, led by Mainland China and Hong Kong (59.2%), Singapore (83.0%), and Taiwan (79.9%). Shipments to other major markets also posted strong gains, including the US (114.3%) and Mexico (94.2%).

title: Slovenia Business Confidence at 2022-Highs
summary: Slovenia's seasonally adjusted manufacturing confidence indicator improved to -2 in July 2026 from -4 in June, marking its least pessimistic reading since August 2022. The improvement was broad-based, while uncertainty eased to its lowest level since October 2025 (30 vs. 33). Production expectations strengthened (13 vs. 7), while the assessment of current production edged up to 5 from 4. Finished goods inventories also increased slightly (3 vs. 2). Order books improved overall (-16 vs. -17) and for exports (-18 vs. -20), while selling price expectations moderated (8 vs. 13). Employment expectations edged up to 8 from 7, although accumulation of labor eased (5 vs. 8). Outside manufacturing, confidence improved in retail trade, was unchanged in construction, and weakened in services, with sentiment in all three sectors remaining above their long-term averages.

title: Bosnia and Herzegovina Inflation at 4-Month Low
summary: The annual inflation rate in Bosnia and Herzegovina eased to 4.2% in June 2026 from 5.6% in the previous month, marking the lowest level since February. Food and non-alcoholic beverage prices fell (-0.5% vs 0.6% in May), as well as for clothing and footwear (-7.2% vs -6.9%). At the same time, inflation eased across several categories, including alcoholic beverages and tobacco (3.4% vs 3.5%), housing and utilities (10.5% vs 11.5%), furnishings, household equipment and routine maintenance (1.1% vs 1.6%), transport (17.5% vs 23.7%), recreation and culture (3.0% vs 3.4%), education (1.8% vs 3.4%), restaurants and hotels (4.9% vs 5.6%), and other goods and services (1.8% vs 2.3%). Meanwhile, inflation held steady for communication at 3.3%, while health inflation edged up (5.7% vs 5.5%). On a monthly basis, consumer prices fell 1.1% in June, following a 0.9% drop in May, marking a second consecutive contraction after eight straight months of increases.

title: Bahrain Inflation Holds Steady at 2.3%
summary: Bahrain’s annual inflation rate stood at 2.3% in June 2026, unchanged from the previous month and remaining at its highest level since May 2024. Prices increased at a faster pace for food and non-alcoholic beverages (5.8% vs 5.7% in May) and transport (10.6% vs 10.4%), while costs for education remained steady at 2.8%. Additionally, deflation eased for alcoholic beverages and tobacco (-0.6% vs -1.3%), clothing and footwear (-12.6% vs -12.7%), and furnishings, household equipment, and routine household maintenance (-1.2% vs -1.3%). In contrast, inflation slowed for miscellaneous goods and services (3.3% vs 3.4%), while prices declined for restaurants and hotels (-0.3% vs 0.2%), communication (-0.3% vs -0.2%), and recreation and culture (-0.6% vs 0.3%). Prices remained unchanged for housing and utilities (-2.2%) and health (-0.2%). On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 0.9% in June from 0.4% in May.

title: SAP Stock Price Hits 6-week High
summary: SAP shares increased to 147.07 EUR, the highest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, SAP gained 7.22%, and in the last 12 months, it decreased 39.97%.

title: South African Rand Recovers as Falling Oil Prices Improve Risk Sentiment
summary: The South African rand strengthened to 16.70 per US dollar, recovering from an over three-month low of 16.98 reached last week, as easing tensions between the US and Iran triggered a sharp drop in oil prices and improved global risk appetite. Brent crude fell from two-month highs after Washington and Tehran paused hostilities following two weeks of strikes, raising hopes for a diplomatic resolution that could de-escalate the conflict and allow shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to resume. Last week, the rand weakened 2% against the dollar after the South African Reserve Bank unexpectedly kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged, against market expectations for a 25-basis-point hike. Meanwhile, South Africa's annual inflation accelerated to 5.0% in June, the highest in two years, while core inflation climbed to 4.1%, its strongest level since September 2024. Both measures remain above the upper end of the SARB's 3% ±1 percentage point target range.

title: Greece Credit Growth at 6-Month High
summary: Total credit extended to the Greek economy rose 5.0% year-on-year in June 2026, accelerating from 4.6% in the previous month and marking the highest growth rate since December 2025. Credit to the private sector also edged higher to 7.7% from 7.4% in May, while the monthly net flow of credit remained positive at €3,288 million, increasing from €1,315 million in the previous month. Meanwhile, credit to the general government increased 0.4% after remaining stagnant in the previous month, with the monthly net flow of credit remaining positive at €213 million, although this was down from €329 million in May.

title: UK Retail Sales Fall The Least Since January
summary: The CBI retail sales balance improved to -26 in July 2026 from -54 in June, well above market expectations of -45, signaling the smallest decline in UK retail sales in six months. Although sales remained lower than a year earlier, retailers said the pace of the downturn had eased, while sales for the time of year were judged to be below seasonal norms by the smallest margin since February. The CBI said the sector continues to face headwinds from weak consumer confidence and elevated cost pressures, leaving the outlook subdued. Looking ahead, retailers' expectations for August improved to -26 from -45, the strongest reading since March. The CBI urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government to support high-street retailers through lower property taxes, address rising labour costs, and preserve hiring flexibility as employment reforms are finalized. Meanwhile, wholesalers reported broadly unchanged sales volumes for the first time in more than two years.

title: Soybeans Fall from Over 2-Year High
summary: Soybeans fell to around $12.13 per bushel, retreating from the more than two-year high of $12.50 reached on July 24, as a sharp decline in crude oil prices weighed on agricultural commodities. Oil tumbled after the US and Iran paused military strikes over the weekend following two weeks of hostilities, boosting hopes that diplomatic efforts could ease tensions and restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the pullback, concerns over global crop supplies persisted. Heatwaves in Europe and continued attacks between Russia and Ukraine have disrupted agricultural trade, including damage to grain infrastructure and shipping routes. Meanwhile, Geneva-based vegetable oil producer Allseeds suspended operations in Ukraine's Odesa region due to intensified attacks on port facilities. However, discussions on measures to safeguard Black Sea shipping have raised hopes that export flows can continue with limited disruption.

title: Wheat Eases from Over 2-Year High
summary: Wheat fell to around $6.70 per bushel, extending losses from the more than two-year high of $7.06 reached on July 22, following a sharp drop in crude oil prices after the United States and Iran paused strikes, raising hopes that diplomatic efforts could de-escalate tensions in the Middle East. Despite the pullback, traders remained focused on risks to global wheat supplies as attacks by Russia and Ukraine in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov regions continued to disrupt grain infrastructure and threaten export flows. Ukrainian authorities reported that air attacks caused casualties in Rostov-on-Don, a major Russian export hub near the Sea of Azov, and in Belgorod, highlighting ongoing tensions around key grain routes. Meanwhile, Allseeds said it was halting operations in Ukraine's southern Odesa region. However, discussions over mechanisms to maintain vessel movements through Ukraine's Black Sea ports have raised hopes that exports may avoid major disruptions.

title: Pakistan Central Bank Holds Policy Rate at 11.5%
summary: The State Bank of Pakistan left its benchmark policy rate unchanged at 11.5% at its July 27th, 2026 meeting, marking a second consecutive pause as policymakers cited an improving macroeconomic outlook. Headline inflation eased to 11.1% in June from 11.7% in May, reflecting lower global energy prices and favorable electricity tariff adjustments. Economic growth slowed to 4.0% in the first quarter of 2026, weighed by the Middle East conflict and the resulting rise in global energy prices. Looking ahead, the central bank expects stronger commodity-producing sectors to support services activity, with FY2027 GDP growth projected at 3.5%-4.5%. Inflation is forecast to gradually ease toward the upper end of the 5%-7% target range by June 2027. However, the outlook remains subject to uncertainty regarding geopolitical tensions and weather conditions, including El Niño effects, and potential fiscal slippages.

title: El Salvador Trade Deficit Widens in June
summary: El Salvador's trade deficit widened to $1,030.96 million on June 2026 from $856.96 million in the same month a year earlier. Imports rose 16.5% year-on-year to $1,628.1 million, driven by purchases from Central America (4.7%), mainly Costa Rica, and Panama (63.5%). Meanwhile, exports rose at a slower pace of 10.5% to $597.2 million, supported by shipments to the UK (38%), Ecuador (25.2%) and Mexico (24.2%). In the January–June 2026 period, the trade deficit widened to $5,919.1 million from $5,302.4 million in the corresponding period a year earlier.

title: US Futures Rebound on Monday
summary: US futures rose on Monday, erasing the losses from last week as drop in energy prices softened worries of a deteriorating macroeconomic backdrop. Contracts for the S&P 500 and the Dow were around 1% higher, while those for the Nasdaq 100 gained nearly 1.5%. The US paused its strikes against Iran over the weekend and benchmark fuel prices eased on hopes that energy exports from the Middle East could return. The consequent drop in yields loosened financial conditions and nearly erased expectations that the Federal Reserve could deliver a rate hike this week, pushing back eventual tightening to September. Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Apple were up premarket ahead of their earnings in the coming days. Nvidia underperformed with a 0.5% gain after a $500 billion AI memory chip supply deal from SK Hynix and guaranteeing $250 billion for OpenAI to lease computing from a data center project, reigniting concerns that circular deals in AI computing could trigger contagion should spending ease.

title: Indian Stocks Rebound
summary: Indian stocks closed sharply higher on Monday after five sessions of losses, as lower oil prices supported the rupee and aided foreign inflows on domestic equities. The S&P/BSE Sensex and the NSE Nifty 50 each gained 1%. The US paused strikes against Iran over the weekend and oil prices trimmed their surge, easing the outlook of rupee selling from energy importers and aiding foreign demand in Indian capital markets. TCS gained 1.9% after reporting stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings. Lodha Developers also climbed following a rise in quarterly profit. Meanwhile, Infosys surged 3% with support from a rebound in the US tech sector. In contrast, Bank of Baroda came under pressure after reporting a decline in quarterly earnings.

title: US Durable Goods Orders Rise Less Than Expected But Core Beat
summary: New orders for US-manufactured durable goods increased 0.3% month-over-month to $334.77 billion in June 2026, rebounding from a revised 4% slump in May but much lower than forecasts of a 1.6% jump. Orders for capital goods went up 1.1% and increases were also seen in orders for primary metals (1.1%), computers and electronics (3.1%), and electrical equipment, appliances, and components (0.9%). On the other hand, orders declined for transportation (-0.2%), mostly motor vehicle and parts (-0.6%), fabricated metal products (-0.5%), and machinery (-0.1%). Excluding transportation, durable goods orders were up 0.6%. Meanwhile, orders for non-defense capital goods excluding aircraft, a closely watched proxy for business spending plans, rose by 0.9%, following an upwardly revised 1.9% rise in May and above forecasts of 0.8%.

title: Mexico Trade Surplus Widens Above Forecasts
summary: Mexico's trade surplus widened to $4.09 billion in June 2026 from $0.51 billion a year earlier, well above market expectations of $2.28 billion. Exports surged 34.4% year-on-year to $72.5 billion, driven by a 34.1% increase in non-oil shipments and a 43.4% rise in oil exports. Manufactured exports climbed 35.3%, led by metal products (40.9%), electrical and electronic equipment (19.7%), food, beverages and tobacco (14.5%), and automotive products (7.6%). In contrast, agricultural and fisheries exports fell 2.8%. Imports rose 28% to $68.46 billion, reflecting strong domestic demand. Intermediate goods imports increased 30.9%, consumer goods imports advanced 23.5%, boosted by a 66% surge in petroleum products, while capital goods imports rose 8.8%.

title: Gold Rebounds as Oil Prices Retreat
summary: Gold rose 1% toward $4,100 an ounce on Monday as easing tensions between the US and Iran sent oil prices sharply lower, easing inflation concerns and reducing fears that the Federal Reserve may need to tighten monetary policy more aggressively ahead of its meeting later this week. Brent crude retreated from two-month highs after Washington and Tehran paused hostilities, raising hopes that a diplomatic resolution could de-escalate the conflict and ensure the safe passage of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran said it would suspend further attacks as long as the US maintained its pause in military operations. Investors now await the Federal Reserve's policy decision on Wednesday. Markets currently assign about a 30% probability of a rate hike this week and roughly an 80% chance of another increase in September.

title: TSX Futures Rise as Oil Prices Tumble
summary: Futures tracking the S&P/TSX Composite Index moved higher on Monday as oil prices tumbled following a pause in hostilities between the US and Iran. Crude prices fell after both countries halted strikes over the weekend amid renewed diplomatic efforts, with President Donald Trump reportedly open to restarting peace talks. The decline in oil prices eased energy-driven inflation concerns, pushing Canadian bond yields lower and supporting financials and the broader market. Gold prices advanced as lower US Treasury yields boosted demand for the metal, supporting mining stocks. Elsewhere, Celestica and Gibson Energy are scheduled to report earnings after the market close.

title: Treasury Yields Retreat
summary: The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note fell to 4.65% on Monday after reaching its highest level since January 2025 last week, helped by declining oil prices. The US suspended its nearly two-week campaign of strikes against Iran late on Friday, although no official announcement was made. As a result, Tehran halted its retaliatory military operations and held talks with Oman on ensuring shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. These developments alleviated concerns over further supply disruptions and a renewed inflationary spiral, prompting investors to scale back expectations for Fed's tightening. Investors are also awaiting the Federal Reserve's monetary policy decision later this week. The central bank is widely expected to leave the federal funds rate unchanged, although markets currently assign roughly a 33% probability to a rate hike. Looking ahead, a September increase remains the base case, with traders pricing in nearly an 80% chance of such a move.

title: Oil Tumbles as US and Iran Halt Strikes
summary: Crude oil fell sharply to as low as $82.11 per barrel on Monday before trimming some losses to trade around $84.30, as signs of easing geopolitical tensions reduced concerns over supply disruptions. The US paused its attacks against Iran, while Tehran said it had halted its retaliatory military strikes in response and engaged in talks with Oman regarding the Strait of Hormuz. Supply conditions also improved after crude loadings resumed at the Caspian Pipeline Consortium terminal on Russia's Black Sea coast, a key export hub for Kazakh oil that had recently been disrupted by Ukrainian drone attacks. Despite Monday's decline, oil remains up more than 20% this month as supply disruptions expanded from the Strait of Hormuz to the Red Sea, an increasingly important alternative route for Saudi Arabian crude exports. Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants claimed to have targeted Saudi Aramco-linked facilities in Jizan and Yanbu, although neither Saudi Arabia nor Aramco confirmed the attacks.

title: Dollar Pares Most Losses
summary: The dollar index pared early losses to trade little changed around 101.4 on Monday, hovering near a one-month high as developments in the Middle East continued to dominate market sentiment. The US suspended its nearly two-week campaign of strikes against Iran late on Friday. In response, Tehran halted its retaliatory military operations and held talks with Oman on ensuring the safe passage of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. These developments triggered a decline in oil prices, easing concerns over further supply disruptions and a renewed inflationary spiral. As a result, investors scaled back expectations for Fed policy tightening. The central bank is widely expected to leave the federal funds rate unchanged, although markets currently assign around a 33% probability to a rate hike. Looking ahead, a September increase remains the base case, with traders pricing in nearly an 80% chance of such a move.

title: US Stocks Rebound on Monday
summary: US stocks rose on Monday, erasing the losses from last week as drop in energy prices softened the deteriorating macroeconomic backdrop. The S&P 500 gained 0.8%, while both the Dow and the Nasdaq 100 rose over 1%. The US paused strikes against Iran over the weekend and benchmark fuel prices eased on hopes that energy exports from the Middle East could return. The consequent drop in yields loosened financial conditions to reflect almost null expectations the Federal Reserve may deliver a rate hike this week, pushing back eventual tightening to September. Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Apple rose up to 2% ahead of their earnings in the coming days. Nvidia underperformed with a 0.5% loss after a $500 billion AI memory chip supply deal from SK Hynix and guaranteeing $250 billion for OpenAI to lease computing from a data center project, reigniting concerns that circular deals in AI computing could trigger contagion and unwind the AI trade should capex growth be halted.

title: Lam Research Stock Price Hits 9-week Low
summary: Lam Research shares decreased to 298.48 USD, the lowest since May 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Lam Research lost 24.78%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 211.74%.

title: Baltic Dry Index Falls on Monday
summary: The Baltic Dry Index declined 1.7% to 2,696 on Monday, ending a three-session winning streak. The Capesize Index, which tracks vessels typically carrying around 150,000 tonnes of bulk commodities such as iron ore and coal, fell 2% to 4,200, its lowest reading since July 23. The Panamax Index, covering ships that usually transport 60,000 to 70,000 tonnes of coal or grain, dropped 1.2% to 1,999, marking its weakest level in eight weeks. Among smaller vessel segments, the Supramax Index decreased 1.4% to 1,670.

title: Ibovespa Rises as Oil Prices Retreat
summary: The Ibovespa edged up to trade above 174,500 on Monday as a pause in the Middle East conflict drove oil prices lower and eased inflation concerns. Crude prices fell after the US and Iran halted strikes over the weekend amid renewed diplomatic efforts, with President Donald Trump reportedly open to restarting peace talks. The pullback in oil prices supported financials, with Itaú and Bradesco each gaining nearly 1%. Utilities also advanced, led by Axia, up more than 2%, while Sabesp gained nearly 1%. WEG rose about 4% after Bradesco BBI upgraded the stock to Outperform and JPMorgan raised its rating to Overweight. The company also secured a contract to supply two generating units for Engie Brasil's Jaguara hydroelectric plant expansion. Embraer climbed more than 3% after reporting a record second-quarter backlog of $34.5 billion. In contrast, Petrobras fell nearly 3% as lower oil prices weighed on the stock.

title: Intuit Stock Price Hits 6-week High
summary: Intuit shares increased to 304.13 USD, the highest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Intuit gained 19.19%, and in the last 12 months, it decreased 61.32%.

title: Corn Falls from 5-Week High
summary: Corn fell toward $4.50 per bushel, moving further away from the five-week high of $4.64 reached on July 24, pressured by a sharp decline in crude oil prices after the US and Iran paused military strikes over the weekend, raising hopes that diplomatic efforts could de-escalate tensions in the Middle East and restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Lower energy prices reduced support for corn as falling crude weakened the outlook for ethanol demand. Meanwhile, improving weather across the US Corn Belt added further pressure, with temperatures expected to ease following the weekend's heat while rainfall is forecast to alleviate dryness and support crop development. Traders also monitored developments in the Black Sea, where efforts to maintain grain shipments through Ukrainian ports helped ease concerns over export disruptions.

title: UnitedHealth Stock Price Hits 4-week Low
summary: UnitedHealth shares decreased to 412.79 USD, the lowest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, UnitedHealth lost 0.48%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 47.14%.

title: TSX Hits Record High as Oil Prices Tumble
summary: The S&P/TSX Composite Index gained 0.5% to trade above 35,500 on Monday, reaching a record high as oil prices tumbled following a pause in hostilities between the US and Iran. Crude prices fell after both countries halted strikes over the weekend amid renewed diplomatic efforts, with President Donald Trump reportedly open to restarting peace talks. The decline in oil prices eased energy-driven inflation concerns, pushing Canadian bond yields lower and supporting financials. RBC, BMO, and CIBC gained about 1%, while TD Bank and Scotiabank added more than 0.5%. Gold prices advanced as lower US Treasury yields boosted demand for the metal, lifting mining stocks. Agnico Eagle, Barrick, and WPM each gained about 1%. Shopify climbed more than 5%, tracking gains in US software stocks. In contrast, energy shares declined on lower oil prices, with Suncor and Cenovus losing nearly 3%. Celestica (+0.3%) and Gibson Energy (-1.2%) are scheduled to report earnings after the market close.

title: Stryker Stock Price Hits 13-week High
summary: Stryker shares increased to 337.15 USD, the highest since April 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Stryker gained 6.45%, and in the last 12 months, it decreased 16.61%.

title: Intel Stock Price Hits 12-week Low
summary: Intel shares decreased to 89.55 USD, the lowest since April 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Intel lost 32.08%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 335.99%.

title: Bristol-Myers Squibb Stock Price Hits 16-month High
summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb shares increased to 63.24 USD, the highest since March 2025. Over the past 4 weeks, Bristol-Myers Squibb gained 7.92%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 33.02%.

title: US Dallas Fed Manufacturing Activity Rises in July
summary: The Dallas Fed's general business activity index for Texas manufacturing rose to 1.3 in July 2026, up from 0 in June. Broader conditions strengthened, with the company outlook index jumping 11 points to 13.4 as uncertainty eased (6.4 vs. 10.9). Manufacturing activity accelerated, with the production index rising to 10.1 from 4.1, supported by stronger new orders (6.4 vs. 2.3) and shipments (8.8 vs. 7.1). Meanwhile, finished goods inventories declined (1.5 vs. 7.8), while delivery times lengthened slightly (2.3 vs. 0.9). Labor market conditions remained broadly stable, although employment (12.2 vs. 13.9) and hours worked (4.3 vs. 5.9) eased, while the wages and benefits index climbed (30.8 vs 25.8). Price pressures remained elevated despite slight moderation in prices paid and received. Looking ahead, firms continue to expect strong manufacturing activity over the next six months, with future production (34.6) and general business activity (26.5) remaining little changed.

title: US Stocks Waver
summary: US stock indices wavered on Monday amid a fresh selloff for chip producers ahead of a Fed decision and major economic updates this week. The S&P 500 swung to 0.3% lower while the Nasdaq 100 dropped 1%. Nvidia dropped 4.5% after announcing a $500 billion AI memory chip supply deal from SK Hynix. Separately, Nvidia guaranteed $250 billion for OpenAI to lease computing from a data center project, reigniting concerns that circular deals in AI computing could trigger contagion and unwind the AI trade should capex growth be halted. Micron, AMD, Indel, and Sandisk dropped between 6% and 10%. Still, the Dow added 0.5% on softer concerns of tight financial conditions. The US and Iran paused strikes over the weekend and fuel prices retreated from peaks. The consequent drop in yields reflected almost null expectations the Federal Reserve may deliver a rate hike this week, pushing back eventual tightening to September. Apple, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft were higher ahead of earnings this week.

title: FX Updates: Norwegian Krone Depreciates by 0.87%
summary: Top currency losers are Norwegian Krone (-0.87%) and South Korean Won (-0.66%). Gains are led by Indian Rupee (0.38%) and Australian Dollar (0.27%). Meanwhile, Euro, Japanese Yen, British Pound and Dollar Index were little changed.

title: FTSE 100 Climbs to 5-Month High
summary: The FTSE 100 gained more than 0.5% on Monday, climbing above 10,800 to its highest level since the record close on February 27, supported by strong corporate earnings and easing energy costs. The US and Iran refrained from further attacks for a third consecutive night, reducing concerns over inflationary pressures. Vodafone was among the strongest performers, rising more than 5% after reporting better-than-expected organic service revenue growth and maintaining a positive outlook. AstraZeneca advanced 2.6% after quarterly earnings exceeded expectations and the company reaffirmed its full-year guidance and 2030 targets. GSK gained more than 3%, while Unilever and BAE Systems also moved higher. In contrast, energy stocks declined as oil prices weakened, with Shell down 1% and BP falling 2.3%. Mining stocks also lagged, including Glencore (-3.3%), Anglo American (-2.4%) and Antofagasta (-1.9%).

title: DAX 40 Rises Toward 3-Week High
summary: The DAX 40 rose more than 1% to above 25,400 on Monday, the highest in nearly three weeks, as improving US-Iran relations, weaker oil prices and falling bond yields boosted investor sentiment. The decline in energy prices eased inflation concerns and reduced expectations for additional monetary tightening ahead of a busy week of central bank decisions and major technology earnings. SAP led the gains, jumping more than 7% after launching the second phase of its €10 billion share buyback programme and extending the positive momentum following stronger-than-expected second-quarter results. Deutsche Telekom (+2.6%) and Rheinmetall (+1.3%) also gained. In contrast, Infineon dropped 4.5% after ASML shares declined following reports that a Chinese state-backed company is developing chipmaking equipment that could challenge its market position. Lower energy prices weighed on Siemens Energy (-2%) and E.ON (-2.5%).

title: European Stocks Inch Higher
summary: European stocks closed slightly higher, outperforming North American counterparts with support from lower bond yields. The Euro STOXX 60 inched higher to 6,290 and the STOXX Europe 600 rose 0.2% to 645.6. Sovereign yields fell sharply as the momentary pause in strikes between Iran and the US reignited hopes of LNG and fuel exports from the region, limiting inflationary risks. Banks were sharply higher, with Santander and BNP Paribas adding over 2% while Intesa Sanapaolo rose 1% ahead of its earnings this week. Meanwhile, software producers jumped, tracking Wall Street counterparts ahead of AI hyperscaler earnings this week, with SAP soaring 7.8%. In turn, chip producers remained volatile and sold off after a series of circular investments by Nvidia added to concerns of overspending on the sector. ASML sank 8.4% and Infineon dropped 4.5%. Also, Argenx dropped 2.3% after buying Forte Biosciences for $2.2 billion.

title: Bonds Update: South Korea 10Y Bond Yield Drops by 11 bps
summary: Government bonds yields are lower on Monday. Top losers are South Korea 10Y (-11.20bps), Japan 10Y (-4.53bps), US 10Y (-3.70bps) and Germany 10Y (-3.42bps).

title: Energy Commodities Updates: Brent Crude Oil Plunges by 10.25%
summary: Top commodity losers are Brent Crude Oil (-10.25%), Natural Gas EU (-9.81%) and Crude Oil WTI (-8.89%). Gains are led by Coking Coal (0.83%).

title: Metals Commodities Updates: Platinum Gains by 1.71%
summary: Top commodity gainers are Platinum (1.71%), Lithium Carbonate (0.69%), Copper (0.65%) and Gold (0.58%). Biggest loser is Iron Ore CNY (-0.67%).

title: Agricultural Commodities Updates: Oat Falls by 4.00%
summary: Top commodity losers are Oat (-4%), Canola (-3.96%) and Cocoa (-3.36%). Gains are led by Coffee (2.89%) and Cotton (1.08%).

title: Crude Oil Near $82
summary: Crude oil extended losses and fell toward $82 per barrel on Monday, its lowest level in a week, as optimism grew that the conflict in the Middle East could soon ease. President Trump said the US was holding "good talks" with Iran and that there was a chance of reaching a deal, but warned that US strikes would resume if negotiations failed. The US paused its military strikes on Iran on Friday, following nearly two weeks of hostilities and Tehran said it had suspended its retaliatory military operations in response and entered talks with Oman regarding navigation through Hormuz. Supply conditions also improved after crude loadings resumed at the Caspian Pipeline Consortium terminal on Russia's Black Sea coast, a key export route for Kazakh oil that had recently been disrupted by Ukrainian drone attacks. Meanwhile, Houthi militants claimed to have targeted Saudi Aramco-linked facilities in Jizan and Yanbu, although neither the Saudi government nor Aramco confirmed it.

title: US Stocks Mixed as Chipmakers Extend Selloff
summary: US stock indices closed mixed on Monday as chipmakers extended their selloff ahead of this week's Fed decision and a busy slate of economic data and corporate earnings. The S&P 500 ended little changed, the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.3%, while the Dow gained 263 points. Nvidia fell 5% after announcing a $500 billion AI memory chip supply agreement with SK Hynix. Separately, the company guaranteed $250 billion for OpenAI to lease computing capacity from a major data center project, reviving concerns that circular AI financing deals could unravel if hyperscalers curb capital spending. Micron (-2.2%), AMD (-5.2%), Intel (-0.7%), and Sandisk (-11%) also declined. Meanwhile, easing concerns over tight financial conditions helped the Dow. The US and Iran paused strikes over the weekend, sending oil prices and Treasury yields lower, easing expectations of a Fed rate hike this week. Apple (+1.2%), Meta (-0.2%), Amazon (-0.3%), and Microsoft (+1.9%) traded mixed ahead of earnings releases.

title: TSX Closes at Record High
summary: The S&P/TSX Composite Index rose 0.6% to a record close of 35,568 on Monday as oil prices tumbled following a pause in hostilities between the US and Iran. Crude prices fell after both countries halted strikes over the weekend amid renewed diplomatic efforts, with President Trump reportedly open to restarting peace talks. The decline in oil prices eased energy-driven inflation concerns, pushing Canadian bond yields lower and supporting financials. CIBC gained 0.8% and Brookfield advanced 1.1%. Gold prices rose as lower US Treasury yields boosted demand for the metal, lifting miners. Agnico Eagle and WPM gained 0.6%, while Barrick added 0.8%. Cameco climbed 1.8% after UBS upgraded the stock to Buy. Technology stocks rallied, with Shopify soaring 11.6%, Constellation Software rising 6.4%, and Celestica gaining 4.5%. Shopify jumped after RBC said the company's software has "great defensibility" against AI-driven disruption. Celestica is scheduled to report earnings after the closing bell.

title: Ibovespa Closes Higher as Oil Prices Retreat
summary: The Ibovespa rose 0.7% to close at 175,335 on Monday as a pause in the Middle East conflict sent oil prices lower and eased inflation concerns. Crude prices fell after the US and Iran halted strikes over the weekend amid renewed diplomatic efforts, with President Trump reportedly open to restarting peace talks. The pullback in oil prices supported financials, with Itaú gaining 1.4%, Bradesco rising 1.2%, and Itaúsa advancing 2%. Utilities moved higher, led by Axia (+2%) and Sabesp (+1.7%). WEG gained 0.9% after Bradesco BBI upgraded the stock to Outperform and JPMorgan raised its rating to Overweight. The company also secured a contract to supply two generating units for Engie's Jaguara hydroelectric plant expansion. Embraer jumped 5.3% after reporting a record second-quarter backlog of $34.5 billion. In contrast, Petrobras fell 2.8% as lower oil prices weighed on the stock. Investors will focus on July's mid-month inflation report on Tuesday for clues on the monetary policy outlook.

title: South Korea Consumer Sentiment Edges Higher
summary: South Korea's Composite Consumer Sentiment Index edged up to 106.8 in July 2026 from 106.6 in June.. Households became slightly more optimistic about future income, with the corresponding index rising to 101 from 100, while expectations for future spending held steady at 110. Sentiment regarding current living standards slipped to 93 from 94, although expectations for future living conditions improved to 98 from 97. Consumers were slightly less optimistic about current domestic economic conditions, with the index falling to 84 from 86, while expectations for the economy over the next six months remained unchanged at 92. Inflation expectations were stable, with households projecting consumer prices to rise 2.7% over the next year, while three- and five-year inflation expectations both stood at 2.6%.

title: NZX 50 Retreats from Record High on Profit-Taking
summary: New Zealand's stocks dropped 44 points, or 0.3%, to 13,806 in Tuesday morning deals, as traders took profit after the index hit a record high a day earlier, buoyed by easing oil prices. Traders remained cautious ahead of the Fed's monetary policy decision and China's PMI data, as well as the release of New Zealand's consumer confidence and business outlook data for July, due this week. However, easing oil prices due to moderating Middle East tensions helped limit the decline, as easing inflation concerns reduced expectations of further interest rate hikes. The broader index was mainly weighed down by losses in the financial, healthcare, industrial, and real estate sectors. Colonial Motor dropped 1.5%, Auckland International Airport fell 1.3%, Infratil decreased 1.2%, Ventia Services Group fell 0.8%, while Fisher & Paykel Healthcare and Henderson Far East Income each shed 0.6%.

title: UK Shop Price Inflation Slows to 7-Month Low
summary: UK shop price inflation rose by 0.9% year-on-year in July 2026, missing market expectations for a 1.2% gain and marking the slowest increase since December 2025. The latest reading also slowed from a 1.2% rise in the previous month, as widespread summer promotions and supermarket discounts curbed price growth. Food inflation slowed to 2.2%, the lowest since February 2025, from 2.4% in the previous month, while non-food inflation eased to 0.2% from 0.6%, despite higher prices for electrical, health, and beauty products due to rising semiconductor and manufacturing costs. On a monthly basis, shop prices fell 0.1%. The British Retail Consortium said retailers intensified discounts on alcohol, snacks, clothing, and footwear during the men's soccer World Cup and summer sales. BRC Chief Executive Helen Dickinson noted that fierce competition continues to limit price increases, though retailers remain under pressure from rising operating costs.

title: Irish Consumer Morale Weakens Slightly
summary: Ireland’s Credit Union Consumer Sentiment Index declined slightly to 61.1 in July 2026 from June’s four-month high of 62.2, the first decline in three months, driven by persistent cost-of-living worries. The index remained well below the long-term survey average of 83.2 but above the 40-month low of 53.3 recorded in April due to a surge in fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. The survey showed that the subindices measuring current conditions, consumer expectations, and the economic outlook all fell slightly. "Concerns about the cost of living continue to outweigh all other economic issues," said Irish League of Credit Unions CEO David Malone. Annual inflation remained elevated at 3.4% in June, driven by rising housing, energy, and education costs, which increased pressure on household budgets.

title: Oil Extends Fall as US-Iran Talks Resume
summary: Crude oil fell toward $81 per barrel on Tuesday, marking a third consecutive session of losses after President Donald Trump said the US was engaged in "good talks" with Iran aimed at ending the Middle East conflict, fueling optimism that normal oil flows from the region could resume. Trump reportedly said he chose to suspend strikes on Iran to give negotiations another chance. The US quietly halted attacks on the Islamic Republic late Friday following nearly two weeks of fighting, while Tehran also ceased retaliatory strikes against US bases in neighboring countries. Meanwhile, Iranian and Omani negotiators met over the weekend in an effort to secure an agreement to restore shipping through the strategically important Strait of Hormuz. Elsewhere, supply conditions also improved as crude exports resumed at the Caspian Pipeline Consortium terminal on Russia's Black Sea coast, a major outlet for Kazakh oil that had recently been disrupted by Ukrainian drone attacks.

title: Dollar Holds Firm Ahead of Fed Meeting
summary: The dollar index traded around 101.5 on Tuesday, holding onto the previous session’s gains as investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s policy decision, with markets pricing in an over one-third chance of a rate hike. Citadel Securities also said it expects the Fed to raise interest rates this week to reinforce Chairman Kevin Warsh’s inflation-fighting credibility after the central bank chief repeatedly pledged to restore price stability. Meanwhile, the probability of a Fed rate hike in September currently stands at around 56%. The dollar also remained resilient even after President Donald Trump said the US was engaged in "good talks" with Iran to end the Middle East conflict, a development that pushed oil prices lower and eased concerns over inflation and tighter monetary policy.

title: Yen Hovers Near 40-Year Lows

Verbal intervention from Japanese authorities has so far done little to support the yen, while the BOJ has remained vague about the pace and timing of any future policy tightening. The currency also stayed under pressure even after President Donald Trump said the US was engaged in "good talks" with Iran to end the Middle East conflict, sending oil prices lower and easing concerns over inflation and tighter monetary policy.

title: South Korean Shares Plunge on Tech Selloff
summary: The benchmark KOSPI plunged more than 8% to around 6,210 on Tuesday, retreating to an over three-month low, as a deepening global semiconductor selloff battered heavyweight chipmakers and fueled broad risk aversion. SK Hynix tumbled over 10% after its US-listed shares fell below their IPO price, while Samsung Electronics slid more than 9%, tracking another decline in US chip stocks amid growing concerns that hyperscalers could rein in AI infrastructure spending. The selloff also dragged down other major shares, including SK Square (-11.8%), Hyundai Motor (-6.8%), LG Energy Solution (-4.7%), HD Hyundai Heavy Industries (-6.3%), and Kia Corporation (-5.0%). Meanwhile, renewed concerns over rising competition from China's memory chip sector added further pressure to Korean semiconductor stocks. Investors also remained cautious ahead of earnings from major US technology companies and the Federal Reserve's policy decision later this week.

title: Taiwan Consumer Sentiment Drops from Four-Month High
summary: Taiwan’s consumer confidence index fell to 64.58 in July 2026 from June’s four-month high of 65.05, reflecting broadly weaker sentiment. Confidence declined across all six core sub-indicators, including domestic economic conditions (80.53 vs 80.87 in June), household finances (77.42 vs 77.70), stock investment prospects (28.08 vs 29.90), durable goods purchases (93.43 vs 93.55), and labor market expectations (72.19 vs 72.46). Other indicators also softened, including the gauge for the timing of real estate purchases (90.13 vs 90.35), current health conditions (86.70 vs 86.82), and expected future health conditions (81.77 vs 81.86).

title: Taiwan Stocks Hit Over 2-Month Low on Tech Selloff
summary: The TAIEX, Taiwan’s benchmark stock index, slumped 1,512 points, or 3.5%, to 42,123 in Tuesday morning trade, down for the third consecutive session and marking its lowest level since May 21, as a global selloff in chipmakers weighed on technology heavyweights. Almost all sectors traded in the red, led by process industries, followed by electronic technology, technology services, and industrial services. Reports that a Chinese state-backed firm began producing immersion DUV lithography equipment and the debut of ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) further pressured sentiment. Electronic technology plunged 3.9%, with TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, accounting for more than 40% of the market's total value, falling 2.6% after being flat in the previous session. Among the biggest decliners were Cambricon Technologies (-2.7%), SMIC (-1.5%), GigaDevice Semiconductor (-7.5%), Zhongji Innolight (-7.1%), and Eoptolink Technology (-6.7%). title: EU Natural Gas Drops Further
summary: European natural gas prices fell to €56.4 per MWh on Tuesday after plunging more than 8% in the previous session, as President Donald Trump expressed optimism about diplomatic efforts to ease tensions with Iran. Trump said on Monday that the US and Tehran were having "good talks" and that there was a chance of reaching a deal, but he warned that US strikes would resume if negotiations failed. His comments followed a pause in hostilities between the two sides to allow room for diplomacy. Despite this, concerns over Europe’s gas supply persist, with the bloc's storage levels at risk of falling short of its winter refill targets. The renewed escalation of the conflict in early July disrupted the recovery of LNG exports from Qatar, the Middle East’s largest LNG supplier, and with the Strait of Hormuz still largely closed, it remains uncertain when additional supplies from the region could reach global markets.

title: EU Natural Gas Rises on Supply Risks
summary: European natural gas prices rose above €57 per MWh on Tuesday, recovering part of the previous session's sharp losses as concerns over Europe's gas supply persisted. The renewed escalation of the conflict in early July disrupted the recovery of LNG exports from Qatar, the Middle East’s largest LNG supplier. With the Strait of Hormuz still largely closed, it remains uncertain when additional supplies from the region could reach global markets, keeping concerns over supply tightness elevated. title: US Natural Gas Hits 3-Month Low
summary: US natural gas futures fell to around $2.72 per MMBtu, extending losses to their lowest level in three months, as strong production, comfortable inventory levels, and weak LNG feedgas demand continue to weigh on prices. Average gas output in the US Lower 48 states rose to 110.6 bcfd so far in July from 110.0 bcfd in June, matching the monthly record high reached in December 2025. The increase in production has added to concerns over an oversupplied market, with inventories remaining 6.4% above the five-year seasonal average as of July 17 and expected to rise to 6.6% above normal for the week ending July 24. LNG export demand also softened, with gas flows to major export terminals averaging 17.2 bcfd so far this month, down slightly from 17.4 bcfd in June, partly due to scheduled maintenance at Freeport LNG’s facility in Texas. Meanwhile, temperatures are forecast to remain mostly above normal through August 11, likely keeping power generators’ gas demand elevated to meet cooling needs.
