Meanwhile, temperatures are forecast to remain mostly above normal through August 11, likely keeping power generators’ gas demand elevated to meet cooling needs.

title: Palm Oil Continues Recent Decline on Weaker Crude Oil
summary: Malaysian palm oil futures remained under pressure, extending recent losses to trade below MYR 4,650 per tonne as weaker rival edible oils on the Dalian and Chicago exchanges weighed on sentiment. Prices moved further away from last week's 15-week high amid a sharp decline in crude oil prices after the U.S. paused strikes on Iran, reducing support by weakening the biodiesel outlook. Still, losses were capped by stronger export demand, with cargo surveyors estimating that July 1–25 palm oil shipments rose between 8.1% and 15.9% from the same period in June. Additional support came from higher biodiesel blending mandates in exporting countries such as Indonesia and Malaysia. Meanwhile, palm oil imports by top buyer India are expected to rise between July and October as tighter edible oil supplies ahead of the festive season boost demand. Weather also remained supportive, with Malaysia warning that record-high temperatures could curb output next year.

title: Australia Underlying Inflation Still Too High: RBA Gov Bullock
summary: Australia's underlying inflation remains too high, and further easing in domestic demand may be needed to bring price growth back to the Reserve Bank's 2%-3% target, Governor Michele Bullock said in a speech on Tuesday. She noted that it remains uncertain whether the three interest rate hikes so far this year will be sufficient, as their full impact has yet to flow through the economy. Bullock warned that underlying inflation could rise further as higher oil prices linked to the Iran conflict feed into broader costs, while noting the labor market also needs to cool further. "The board is prepared to act as required to achieve its mandate, including by increasing the cash rate further if needed," she said. Meanwhile, the recent surge in oil prices highlights the uncertainty from the Middle East war, with more businesses indicating they intend to pass higher costs on to consumers. Bullock added that growth is slowing as expected while the housing market weakened more than anticipated.

title: Malaysia Producer Prices Rise the Most in Four Years
summary: Malaysia’s producer prices climbed 9.2% year-on-year in June 2026, accelerating from a 7.8% increase in May and marking the fourth consecutive month of growth. It was also the strongest annual rise since June 2022, as producer cost pressures intensified amid supply disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict. Manufacturing prices accelerated sharply (7.2% vs. 3.5% in May), driven by higher costs for coke & refined petroleum products (30.1%) and computer, electronic & optical products (8.3%). The agriculture sector remained resilient (9.1% vs. 8.9%), supported by fishing (12.5%) and perennial crops (10.8%). Utilities also posted solid gains, with water supply (10.2% vs. 10.0%) and electricity & gas (12.7% vs. 11.2%) continuing to strengthen. Meanwhile, mining growth slowed markedly (29.0% vs. 52.6%), although crude petroleum extraction remained robust (40.7%). On a monthly basis, the producer price index rose 0.6%, easing from a 1.1% increase in May.

title: Kyrgyz Central Bank Stands Pat at 12%
summary: The National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 12.0% at its July 27, 2026 meeting, maintaining tight monetary conditions to contain persistent inflationary pressures. Inflation rose 6.5% since the start of 2026, with annual inflation reaching 11.3%, driven by higher food and fuel prices amid volatility in global commodity markets and heightened tensions in the Middle East. The central bank warned that risks to oil product supplies through the Strait of Hormuz continue to fuel imported inflation, while rising service costs have also been supported by tax reforms. Meanwhile, the economy remained resilient, with real GDP expanding 11.9% year-on-year, supported by strong domestic demand and robust investment, particularly in construction. The bank reaffirmed that it will maintain restrictive monetary conditions to steer inflation toward its 5%–7% medium-term target and stands ready to tighten policy further if risks to price stability intensify.

title: Rupiah Nears IDR 18,100 as Markets Assess Fed and BI Leadership Risks
summary: The Indonesian rupiah slid toward IDR 18,100 per dollar on Tuesday, marking a second day of losses as the greenback stayed firm ahead of the Fed’s policy decision later this week. Domestically, sentiment was unsettled after Governor Perry Warjiyo resigned, with Senior Deputy Destry Damayanti stepping in as acting chief until a permanent successor is named. The leadership change comes at a fragile moment, with fiscal strains, doubts over the government’s agenda, and fading foreign investor confidence weighing on Indonesian assets. Concerns over central bank independence also lingered after President Prabowo appointed his nephew to the BI’s board. Traders now look to the upcoming securities auctions for signals of the central bank’s resolve to aid the rupiah. Last week, the board surprised markets by holding its key rate at 5.75%, despite expectations for another hike following 100bps of tightening since May. The rupiah has lost near 8% this year, ranking among Asia’s weakest currencies.

title: Indian Stocks Edge Lower
summary: India’s BSE Sensex fell about 0.1% to 76,741 on Tuesday, giving back some of the previous session’s gains after snapping a five-session losing streak. Indian equities were expected to trade in a narrow range as investors awaited the US Federal Reserve’s policy decision and its assessment of the inflationary impact of the Iran conflict on the US economy, a key focus for India’s IT sector, which derives a significant share of its revenue from the US. Among individual stocks, Bharat Electronics and Tata Power were in focus after reporting strong quarterly earnings. Coal India came under pressure after missing earnings estimates due to weaker volumes and higher costs, while InterGlobe Aviation was in focus after appointing Kiran Thadimarri as its new chief financial officer. Among the laggards were Godfrey (-6.3%), CG Power (-5.0%), HFCL (-4.7%), Himadri Specialty (-3.5%), and Bharat Electronics (-3.2%).

title: Euro Hits 4-week Low
summary: EURUSD decreased to 1.14, the lowest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Euro US Dollar lost 0.51%, and in the last 12 months, it decreased 1.62%.

title: FX Updates: Australian Dollar Depreciates by 0.29%
summary: Top currency losers are Australian Dollar (-0.29%) and Euro (-0.06%). Meanwhile, Dollar Index, British Pound and Japanese Yen were little changed.

title: NZX 50 Rebounds, Ends at New Record High
summary: New Zealand's stocks ticked up 11 points, or 0.1%, to close at 13,862 on Tuesday, reversing morning losses, buoyed by gains in healthcare, communication services, industrials, and consumer staples. The broader index hit a new record high, marking its second consecutive record close, after closing at 13,851 a day earlier. Easing oil prices continued to lift sentiment as easing inflation concerns reduced expectations of further interest rate hikes. However, a decline in US stock futures limited the gains amid a global tech selloff. Traders also remained cautious ahead of the Fed's monetary policy decision and China's PMI data, as well as the release of New Zealand's consumer confidence and business outlook data for July, due this week. Among the best performers were AFT Pharmaceuticals (5.2%), Fisher & Paykel Healthcare (2.2%), Auckland International Airport (1.0%), Australian Foundation Investment (0.8%), ANZ Group (0.7%), F&C Investment Trust (0.7%), and a2 Milk (0.6%).

title: European Stocks Set for Lower Open
summary: European equity markets were set to open lower on Tuesday as investor sentiment weakened amid a global selloff in semiconductor stocks, fueled by mounting concerns over circular artificial intelligence financing arrangements and intensifying competition from China. The declines came even as oil prices extended their losses after President Donald Trump said the US was engaged in "good talks" with Iran aimed at ending the Middle East conflict. In Europe, investors will monitor French consumer confidence and employment data, along with unemployment and retail sales figures from Spain. On the corporate front, earnings reports are due from Unilever, Safran, Air Liquide, GlaxoSmithKline, and Essilor, among others. In premarket trading, Euro Stoxx 50 and Stoxx 600 futures were both down about 0.2%.

title: Danish Retail Sales Hit 3-Month High
summary: Retail sales in Denmark rose 4.8% year-on-year in June 2026, accelerating from a downwardly revised 3.7% increase in the previous month and marking the strongest growth since March. Sales grew at a faster pace for consumer electronics (17.4% vs 5.7% in May), household equipment, furniture, and building materials (11.2% vs 4.9%), clothing, footwear, and jewelry (11.6% vs 8.1%), and pharmaceuticals and personal care products (4.9% vs 3.2%). Moreover, sales declined at a slower pace for liquid fuel filling stations (-17.2% vs -19.1%). On the other hand, growth moderated for supermarkets, department stores, and specialized grocery stores (1.6% vs 3.0%), cultural and leisure products (13.2% vs 17.6%), and second-hand goods (10.9% vs 13.2%). On a seasonally adjusted monthly basis, retail sales increased 0.5%, easing from a 1.0% rise in May.

title: TAIEX Slumps 4.7%, Ends at Over 2-Month Low
summary: The TAIEX, Taiwan’s benchmark stock index, plunged 2,031 points, or 4.7%, to 41,603 on Tuesday, retreating for the third consecutive session and marking its lowest level since May 21, as a global selloff in chipmakers weighed on technology heavyweights. Reports that a Chinese state-backed firm began producing immersion DUV lithography equipment and the debut of ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) further pressured sentiment. Electronic technology slumped 5.3%, with TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, accounting for more than 40% of the market's total value, falling 3.0% after being flat in the previous session. Meanwhile, Delta Electronics and MediaTek plunged 10.0% and 9.9%, respectively. Among the major memory chip suppliers, Nanya Technology Corp. and Winbond Electronics Corp. each plunged 10.0%. On the data front, Taiwan's consumer confidence weakened in July from June's four-month high.

title: Taiwan 10Y Yield Jumps on Rate Hike Bets
summary: Taiwan's 10-year government bond yield climbed to around 1.88% in late July, its highest level since October 2022, as investors increasingly priced in the prospect of tighter monetary policy. Expectations for higher interest rates have strengthened after inflation remained above the central bank's 2% target in recent months, reinforcing the view that policymakers may need to keep monetary conditions restrictive or consider further tightening if price pressures persist. However, the central bank has continued to stress that future policy decisions will remain data dependent. Rising bond yields have also been supported by the central bank's liquidity withdrawals to curb depreciation of the Taiwan dollar and strong investor interest in AI-related equities. The move has been accompanied by a broader selloff across the bond market, with the 20-year bond yield reaching its highest level since 2014 and the five-year yield climbing to its highest level since 2008.

title: Lithuania Retail Sales Growth at 4-Month Low
summary: Retail sales in Lithuania rose 5.8% year-on-year in June 2026, easing from a revised 6.9% increase in the previous month and marking the weakest growth rate since February. Sales growth moderated in retail trade excluding automotive sales (9.3% vs 9.6% in May), non-food products (12.5% vs 14.3%), particularly textiles, clothing, and footwear (11.4% vs 12.7%), audio, video, hardware, furniture, and lighting (14.4% vs 16.4%), and information and communication equipment, cultural and recreation goods, watches and jewellery (2.6% vs 5.1%). At the same time, retail activity via mail order houses or the internet slowed (14.6% vs 19.8%), while sales of automotive fuel declined further (-6.9% vs -3.5%). Conversely, sales rose for other goods in non-specialized stores (34% vs 24.1%) food, beverages, and tobacco (4.7% vs 3.1%), and pharmaceuticals, medical goods, and cosmetics (11.9% vs 10.4%). On a monthly basis, retail sales grew 0.3% in June, rebounding from a revised 1% decline in May.

title: Sweden Trade Surplus Shrinks in June
summary: Sweden posted a trade surplus of SEK 2.6 billion in June 2026, more than four times lower than the SEK 11.8 billion recorded in the same month a year earlier, as imports rose faster than exports. Imports climbed by 18.1% year-on-year to an all-time high of SEK 195.3 billion, driven by higher purchases from both EU markets (21% to SEK 131.8 billion) and non-EU countries (12.6% to SEK 63.5 billion). Meanwhile, exports grew at a slower pace of 11.7%, but also to a record of SEK 197.6 billion, reflecting increased shipments to both EU countries (18.2% to SEK 112.2 billion) and non-EU countries (4.3% to SEK 85.7 billion). Considering the first six months of the year, the country’s trade surplus narrowed sharply to SEK 8.2 billion from SEK 47.9 billion in the corresponding period a year ago, as exports rose 3%, while imports increased by a faster 7%. On a seasonally adjusted basis, the trade net recorded a deficit of SEK 0.5 billion in June.

title: Iron Ore Falls on Signs of Ample Supply
summary: Iron ore futures dropped toward CNY 740 per ton, hovering near three-week lows as evidence of abundant global supply continued to pressure prices. Imported iron ore inventories at Chinese ports remained high, while stockpiles at Chinese steel mills climbed 8% last week. Data also showed that Western Australia’s Pilbara Ports, the world’s largest iron ore export hub, handled more than 800 million tons of cargo during the 2025-2026 financial year, with iron ore shipments totaling about 759.4 million tons. That surpassed the previous record of 775.7 million tons set in the 2024-2025 financial year. Meanwhile, Port Hedland handled 580.4 million tons of cargo over the same period, while Dampier processed 178.3 million tons. On the demand side, investors are awaiting updates from the Politburo meeting in Beijing for potential stimulus measures that could provide support to the Chinese economy.

title: Lithuania Industrial Output Rebounds Sharply in June
summary: Industrial production in Lithuania surged 9.8% year-on-year in June 2026, rebounding sharply from a 1.6% fall in the previous month. This marked the strongest expansion since July 2024, driven by renewed growth in manufacturing output excluding refined petroleum products (11.5% vs -1.0% in May) and a sharp increase in mining and quarrying activity (9.1% vs 1.7%). The pace of decline also moderated in the electricity, gas, steam, and air conditioning supply sector (-3.1% vs -9.5%) as well as in water supply, sewerage, waste management, and remediation services (-8.6% vs -13.3%). On a seasonally adjusted monthly basis, industrial output rose 2.1%, recovering from a 2.9% drop in May.

title: Philippine Peso Trades Near Record Low
summary: The Philippine peso traded around 61.7 per US dollar in late July, hovering near its record low as the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas maintained only limited intervention in the foreign exchange market and signaled that aggressive monetary tightening remained unlikely. The central bank intervened modestly last week to maintain orderly market conditions, with Governor Eli Remolona stressing that aggressively defending the peso against a strong US dollar would only deplete the country's foreign exchange reserves. While authorities remain concerned that the peso's weakness could fuel imported inflation, Remolona said the likelihood of aggressive rate hikes to bring inflation back to target remains small. Broad US dollar strength and elevated crude oil prices, which have weighed on Asia's oil-importing economies, have kept the peso under pressure, leaving the currency down more than 7% against the greenback so far this year.

title: ASX 200 Reverses Early Losses to Finish Higher
summary: The ASX 200 rose 54 points, or 0.6%, to close at 8,948 on Tuesday, rebounding from early weakness and marking a second straight gain. Sentiment brightened after U.S. President Trump said Washington was having “good talks” with Iran and that a deal was possible, easing fears of supply disruptions and sending oil prices lower. Locally, Australia is weighing its first new oil refinery in over six decades as the Middle East war squeezes supplies. Gains were broad-based, led by commercial services, healthcare, transport, and financials. The big four banks were up between 0.7% and 1.2%. Also, Sonic Healthcare rose 2.2%, along with Sigma Healthcare (1.8%), and Ramsay Health (1.2%). In contrast, Origin Energy edged lower after flagging possible data exposure affecting about 900,000 customers in a cybersecurity incident. Traders now await Australia’s June and Q2 inflation reports due Wednesday, with sticky price pressures still in focus despite three rate hikes by the Reserve Bank this year.

title: France Consumer Confidence Improves in July
summary: The consumer confidence indicator in France rose to 86 in July 2026, a four-month high, up from 84 in June, but remained below its long-term average of 100. Consumers became less pessimistic about both their past financial situation (-26 vs -28 in June) and expected financial situation (-14 vs -16), while sentiment toward France's future standard of living improved sharply (-59 vs -65) and views on past living standards also became less negative (-79 vs -81). Pessimism over major purchase intentions also eased (-36 vs -38), while saving intentions (45 vs 41) and both current (19 vs 16) and expected (17 vs 14) saving capacity increased. Households' fears of unemployment cooled (55 vs 61) but remained above their long-term average. Meanwhile, the savings climate index rebounded to 123, while inflation expectations dropped sharply (-33 vs -15), returning close to their pre-Middle East conflict level.

title: Australian Dollar Slips on RBA Remarks
summary: The Australian dollar depreciated to below $0.698, easing from multi-week highs as investors reassessed the monetary policy outlook after fresh comments from the central bank's governor. Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock said another interest rate hike may still be needed to bring inflation back to target, but stressed that the near-term outlook remains highly uncertain. She noted that further moderation in domestic demand and labor market conditions would likely be needed before policymakers can judge whether previous tightening has been sufficient. Her comments led markets to trim the probability of an August rate hike to around 20% from about 30%, though investors continue to expect the cash rate to reach 4.60% by year-end. Focus now turns to Wednesday's second-quarter CPI report, with core inflation expected to accelerate to 3.7%, remaining above the RBA's 2%–3% target range. Meanwhile, a pause in US-Iran hostilities provided support for the risk-sensitive Aussie.

title: Unilever Stock Price Hits 18-week High
summary: Unilever shares increased to 4878.00 GBp, the highest since March 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Unilever gained 1.03%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 4.49%.

title: Air Liquide Stock Price Hits 4-week Low
summary: Air Liquide shares decreased to 171.49 EUR, the lowest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Air Liquide lost 0.46%, and in the last 12 months, it decreased 1.94%.

title: AXA Stock Price Hits 9-1/2-year High
summary: AXA shares increased to 45.54 EUR, the highest since December 2016. Over the past 4 weeks, AXA gained 4.62%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 7.7%.

title: UK Gas Prices Extend Decline
summary: UK natural gas prices dropped below 136 pence per therm on Tuesday after tumbling more than 8% in the previous session, as President Donald Trump expressed optimism about diplomatic efforts to ease tensions with Iran. Trump said on Monday that the US and Tehran were having "good talks" and that there was a chance of reaching a deal, but he warned that US strikes would resume if negotiations failed. His comments followed a pause in hostilities between the two sides to allow room for diplomacy. Despite this, concerns over Europe’s gas supply persist, with the bloc's storage levels at risk of falling short of its winter refill targets. The renewed escalation of the conflict in early July disrupted the recovery of LNG exports from Qatar, the Middle East’s largest LNG supplier, and with the Strait of Hormuz still largely closed, it remains uncertain when additional supplies from the region could reach global markets.

title: Airbus Stock Price Hits 27-week High
summary: Airbus shares increased to 212.10 EUR, the highest since January 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Airbus gained 10.32%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 17.78%.

title: Spain Retail Sales Growth Slows to 2-Year Low
summary: Retail sales in Spain increased 0.5% year-on-year in June 2026, the lowest since June 2024, following a 1.3% rise in the previous month. Sales growth eased for non-food products (2.8% vs 3.8% in May), particularly personal equipment (1.5% vs 3.4%) and household equipment (2.9% vs 6.2%). Spending on food also slowed (0.3% vs 1.9%). On the other hand, sales growth accelerated for healthcare products (2.8% vs 2.5%). On a seasonally adjusted monthly basis, retail trade increased by 0.3% in June, after a 0.6% rise in May.

title: Nickel Falls from Over 1-Month High
summary: Nickel fell to around $17,030 per tonne in late July, retreating from an over one-month high near $17,300, as investors locked in profits following a strong rally in recent weeks. Prices also came under pressure after Indonesia moved to resolve regulatory bottlenecks that had delayed exports of some nickel products, easing concerns over near-term supply disruptions. The move followed reports that the government is working to address uncertainty over the allowable rare-earth content in mineral shipments, which had disrupted exports of nickel products and alumina. Still, losses were limited by signs of tighter market conditions, with LME nickel inventories declining for six consecutive sessions, while support from Indonesian mining policies and slower nickel ore shipments from the Philippines had helped lift prices.

title: Euro Drops to One-Month Low as Fed Rate Outlook Supports Dollar
summary: The euro slipped below $1.14, touching its weakest point in a month, as investors continued to monitor developments in the Middle East while the dollar found support from lingering expectations that the Federal Reserve could still raise interest rates on Wednesday. Although a pause in US attacks on Iran pushed oil prices lower and eased inflation concerns, US Treasury yields retreated only modestly, reflecting continued caution. In Europe, money markets slightly pared expectations for additional ECB tightening but still price in nearly two 25 bp rate hikes by March 2027. ECB policymaker Peter Kazimir said at least one more rate increase will likely be needed to curb inflation, adding that a weaker economic outlook could justify even more tightening than markets currently anticipate, while Chief Economist Philip Lane said the current inflation shock remains moderate, supporting further policy tightening. Investors now await fresh inflation data later this week for further policy clues.

title: European Stocks Rise, Earnings in Focus
summary: The STOXX 50 rose 0.3% and the STOXX 600 gained 0.1% on Tuesday, with investors focusing on a fresh round of corporate earnings and welcoming a further decline in oil prices as the pause in hostilities between the US and Iran appeared to hold. LVMH advanced 2.6% after reporting broadly in-line sales growth. Unilever jumped 5% after raising its full-year sales guidance, while Mercedes-Benz climbed 4.3% after posting a profit beat despite a sharp drop in deliveries in China. Orange also gained 3.1% after upgrading its annual profit outlook. On the downside, Barclays fell 4.9% and Safran slipped 1% as their earnings reports failed to impress investors. Meanwhile, the technology sector remained under pressure globally, with renewed concerns over AI-related spending weighing particularly on semiconductor stocks. ASML extended its recent losses, falling 0.5%, after reports that a Chinese state-backed company has started mass-producing certain chipmaking equipment.

title: DAX Hits Three-Week High as Mercedes Rallies, Oil Prices Ease
summary: Frankfurt's DAX 40 gained 0.6% to 25,520 on Tuesday, its highest level since July 6, as investors welcomed corporate earnings updates and lower oil prices amid hopes the US and Iran could resume negotiations to ease tensions in the Middle East. Mercedes-Benz surged more than 5% to lead the index after reaffirming its passenger car margin target despite cutting its revenue forecast following a weak quarter. Meanwhile, TeamViewer fell over 2% after reporting another decline in revenue while maintaining its full-year guidance. AI-related stocks remained under pressure as concerns grew that the sector's rally has become overstretched, alongside rising competition from China and increasing funding requirements. Infineon and Siemens Energy both slipped around 1%, while Hochtief dropped 3%, with the construction firm exposed through its US subsidiary Turner to slowing enthusiasm around large data center projects.

title: Spain Jobless Rate at 2008-Lows
summary: The unemployment rate in Spain fell to 9.87% in the second quarter of 2026, the lowest since the first quarter of 2008, compared to 10.83% in the previous period and forecasts of 10.7%. The number of unemployed persons declined by 213,300 to 2.495 million, with unemployment falling in all sectors: services (-170,300), agriculture (-22,400), industry (-10,900) and construction (-5,400). Unemployment fell by 57,700 among people who had been out of work for more than a year, while it increased by 53,400 among first-time job seekers. By gender, the number of unemployed men fell by 67,900 while the number of unemployed women declined by 145,400. The female unemployment rate dropped to 11.02%, while the male unemployment rate fell to 8.84%. Meanwhile, employment increased by 486,00 to 22.779 million, rising in services (+394,000), construction (+60,000) and industry (+38,200) while falling in agriculture (-6,200).

title: Pound Falls to One-Month Low as Fed Outlook Boosts Dollar
summary: The British pound fell below $1.33, its weakest level in nearly a month, as investors tracked developments in the Middle East while the US dollar gained support from lingering expectations that the Federal Reserve could still raise interest rates on Wednesday. Although a pause in US attacks on Iran pushed oil prices lower and eased inflation concerns, US Treasury yields declined only modestly, reflecting persistent market caution. Investors are also awaiting the Bank of England's policy decision later this week, with markets widely expecting interest rates to remain unchanged at 3.75%. Recent inflation data has reinforced that outlook, with annual consumer price growth slowing to a 15-month low of 2.6% in June, below the BoE's projections. A delayed pass-through of higher wholesale energy prices to regulated household bills has kept UK inflation below levels seen in the US and the euro area, where central banks are still expected to raise interest rates in September or October.

title: South Africa Leading Index Falls 0.3% MoM
summary: The composite leading business cycle indicator in South Africa dropped by 0.3% month-over-month in May 2026, following an upwardly revised 2.0% fall in the previous month. This marked the second consecutive monthly contraction, reflecting weakness in five of the ten available component time series, which outweighed improvements in the other five components. The latest reading was driven largely by weaker business confidence, fewer building plans approved for flats, townhouses and larger houses, and lower commodity prices for South Africa’s main export products. Additional pressure came from shorter average hours worked per factory worker in manufacturing and a narrower interest rate spread between 10-year government bonds and 91-day Treasury bills. Meanwhile, gains in real M1 money supply growth, new passenger vehicle sales, domestic manufacturing orders, job advertisements, and improved conditions among South Africa’s major trading partners provided some support.

title: Energy Commodities Updates: Brent Crude Oil Falls by 2.43%
summary: Top commodity losers are Brent Crude Oil (-2.43%), Natural Gas UK (-2.30%) and Crude Oil WTI (-1.60%).

title: Metals Commodities Updates: Silicon Drops by 1.33%
summary: Top commodity losers are Silicon (-1.33%), Silver (-1.31%), Platinum (-0.89%) and Gold (-0.53%).

title: Agricultural Commodities Updates: Rice Drops by 2.61%
summary: Top commodity losers are Rice (-2.61%), Palm Oil (-0.92%) and Cotton (-0.90%).

title: FTSE 100 Edges Up, Unilever Surges
summary: The FTSE 100 traded modestly higher on Tuesday, with strong gains in consumer stocks offsetting weakness in banks and energy shares. Unilever surged more than 6% after the consumer goods group reported better-than-expected results, driven by robust performance in the US and emerging markets, while also raising its outlook for 2026. Barclays was among the biggest laggards, falling more than 5% despite reporting a 16% increase in second-quarter group income. The lender benefited from strong investment banking and US consumer operations amid heightened market volatility, but the results prompted profit-taking and weighed on the broader banking sector. Energy stocks also remained under pressure as oil prices extended recent losses. Shell slipped 0.8% and BP eased 0.4% after US President Donald Trump said there was a good chance of reaching an agreement with Iran, raising expectations of easing geopolitical tensions and reducing concerns over potential disruptions to global crude supplies.

title: Lumber Slips from One-Year High
summary: Lumber prices fell below $650 per thousand board feet after reaching a near one-year high, as new U.S. tariffs on most Canadian wood-related products weighed on the market. Although Canadian softwood lumber was exempt from Washington's new 50% tariffs, 98 other wood-product categories remained subject to the duties, deflating hopes of a lumber carve-out. Meanwhile, the Canadian government announced additional financial support for lumber producers in Western Canada to help offset tariffs and trade uncertainty. The Forest Products Association of Canada described the measures as a direct blow to the country's forestry sector, where mills are already operating below capacity, as Canadian duties of nearly 35% on lumber forced production cuts and mill closures. Still, wildfires across Western Canada continued to threaten lumber availability, while President Donald Trump warned that wildfire-related costs could be incorporated into existing duties.

title: Slovenia Retail Sales Hit 4-Month Low
summary: Slovenia's retail sales rose 2.1% year-on-year in June 2026, easing slightly from an upwardly revised 2.2% increase in the previous month and marking the weakest growth since February. The slowdown was driven by a 1.8% increase in retail sale of automotive fuel in specialised stores. Meanwhile, food climbed 1.6, while non-food retail sales grew 1.5%. On a seasonally adjusted monthly basis, retail sales fell 0.2% in June, reversing an upwardly revised 0.1% gain in May. In the first half of 2026, retail turnover was 1.9% from the same period a year earlier, supported by a 6.4% jump in motor fuel sales and a 2.5% rise in non-food retail sales. By contrast, food retail sales declined 0.9%, underscoring continued softness in consumer demand for food products.

title: FX Updates: Norwegian Krone Depreciates by 0.39%
summary: Top currency loser is Norwegian Krone (-0.39%). Gains are led by Brazilian Real (0.26%) and British Pound (0.10%). Meanwhile, Dollar Index, Japanese Yen and Euro were little changed.

title: Dollar Index Hits 4-week High
summary: DXY increased to 101.60, the highest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Dollar Index gained 0.48%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 2.74%.

title: Macedonia Producer Inflation Hits Over 1-Year High
summary: The annual producer inflation rate in North Macedonia rose to 6.2% in June 2026 from a 6.0% increase in the previous month, marking the highest level since March 2025. Price growth continued for energy (10.9% vs 10.2% in May), intermediate goods excluding energy (4.7% vs 4.5%), and consumer goods (3.7% vs 3.0%), particularly non-durable goods (3.7% vs 2.9%). Meanwhile, prices eased for capital goods (10.6% vs 11.2%). By sectors and divisions, costs edged up in manufacturing (5.2% vs 5.1%), while inflation rose for mining and quarrying (24.5% vs 23.2%), electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply (11.2% vs 10.7%), and water supply, sewerage, waste management and remediation services (7.4% vs 6.4%). On a monthly basis, producer prices edged up 0.5% in June, down from 1.2% in May.

title: French Unemployment Rises in June
summary: France's registered unemployment rose by 5,900 to 3,121.5 thousand in June 2026, slowing from a 15,500 increase in May. The monthly increase was driven primarily by older job seekers, with the number of unemployed individuals aged 50 and over climbing by 5,400 to 779,800. Meanwhile, unemployment among those under 25 rose by 1,500 to 509,400, while the number of job seekers aged 25 to 49 declined by 1,000 to 1.812 million. By gender, registered unemployment among men increased by 7,400 to 1.622 million, more than offsetting a decline of 1,500 among women, whose total fell to 1.500 million.

title: Ireland Retail Activity Growth Holds Steady
summary: Retail sales in Ireland rose by 0.4% month-on-month in June 2026, matching the pace recorded in the previous month. The largest volume increases were recorded in electrical goods (+1.8%), clothing, footwear, and textiles (+1.5%), bars (+1.2%), books, newspapers, and stationery (+1.2%). Fuel sales also strengthened, rising 6.0% in value and 0.4% in volume, reflecting elevated fuel prices amid ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Meanwhile, gains were partly capped by notable declines in furniture and lighting (-1.8%) and pharmaceuticals, medical, and cosmetic articles (-1.4%). On an annual basis, retail activity grew by 0.6% in June, easing from an upwardly revised 0.9% rise in the preceding period.

title: Crude Falls for 3rd Session
summary: Crude oil fell to around $81 per barrel on Tuesday, touching its lowest level in more than a week, as optimism over a potential diplomatic breakthrough between the US and Iran eased concerns about supply disruptions. President Donald Trump said Washington was engaged in “good talks” with Tehran and that there was a “good chance” of reaching a resolution after pausing military strikes to give negotiations more time. He cautioned, however, that US attacks would resume if diplomacy failed, while Iran also warned it would retaliate should talks collapse. Oman has reportedly proposed a joint regional mechanism to manage shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, including a voluntary fee system. Despite the improving diplomatic outlook, geopolitical risks remain elevated. Saudi Arabia said it intercepted drones launched from Iraq targeting petroleum facilities, blaming Iran-backed groups, while Yemen’s Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for an attack on Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline.

title: India Industrial Production Grows Most in 2 Years
summary: Industrial production in India expanded by 7.3% from the previous year in June of 2026, firmly above market expectations of a 5.7% growth rate to mark the sharpest pace of expansion in nearly two years. The result consolidated the rebound from lower growth rates in the start of the second quarter, when the war in the Middle East triggered energy shortages and lifted input costs for power-intensive industries. Manufacturing production surged by 7.8%, the most since the start of the year. In the meantime, output continued to surge for electricity and gas supply (10.6% vs 10.3% in May) and rebounded for mining and quarrying (1.0% vs -1.4%). From the previous month, industrial output expanded by 0.5%.

title: Brazil Current Account Deficit Narrows More Than Expected
summary: Brazil's current account deficit narrowed to $2.33 billion in June 2026 from $5.18 billion in the same month a year earlier, beating market expectations of a $2.45 billion shortfall. The improvement was largely driven by a stronger trade balance, with the surplus widening by $3.6 billion to $8.8 billion as goods exports surged 24.8% year-on-year to a record $36.4 billion, while imports rose 15.3% to $27.6 billion. Primary and secondary income balances were broadly unchanged from a year earlier, with the primary income deficit holding at $6.5 billion and the secondary income surplus edging up to $438 million. Meanwhile, the services deficit widened by $0.7 billion to $5.1 billion, reflecting higher net spending on international travel (21%), transportation (22.4%), and telecommunications, computing, and information services (16.9%).

title: North Macedonia Holds Key Policy Rate at 4.25%
summary: The National Bank of North Macedonia left its interest rate unchanged at 4.25% at its July 2026 meeting, citing uncertainty surrounding foreign prices and geopolitical tensions. Although headline inflation slowed in June to 3.4% from 4.8%, driven by lower food prices, policymakers stated more time was needing to assess price stability considering that inflation remains elevated, as foreign prices are still high and unstable due to geopolitical tensions and possible spill-over effects. Economic activity continues to show resilience, although growth slowed to 3.1% in the first quarter of 2026 from 3.8% in the prior quarter. Looking ahead, the NBNM stated it will continue to aim for stability of the denar against the euro, in order to ensur price stability in the medium term, and will closely monitor domestic and international economic and financial development.

title: Brazil Mid-Month Inflation Comes in Below Forecasts
summary: Consumer prices in Brazil rose 0.06% in the month to mid-July 2026, slowing sharply from 0.41% in June and coming in below forecasts of 0.2%. The reading marked the lowest mid-month inflation rate since August 2025. Food and beverage prices provided the largest downward contribution, falling 0.66%. Food consumed at home dropped 1.14%, while food away from home accelerated to 0.55%. Housing was the main source of inflationary pressure, rising 0.97%, driven by a 3.03% increase in residential electricity prices following the introduction of the yellow tariff flag and regulated tariff adjustments in several cities. Transportation prices rose 0.11%, as an 11.7% jump in airfares more than offset lower fuel prices amid easing concerns over the Middle East oil supply crisis. Health and personal care costs increased 0.28%, led by higher personal hygiene product prices. The 12-month inflation rate eased to 4.52% from 4.58% in June.

title: US Wholesale Inventories Rise More than Expected
summary: US wholesale inventories rose 0.3% month-over-month to $945.9 billion in June 2026, matching an upwardly revised 0.3% increase in May and exceeding market expectations of a 0.2% gain. According to preliminary data, inventories increased for a fifth consecutive month, supported by a 0.7% rise in durable goods stocks after a 0.2% increase in the previous month. Meanwhile, nondurable goods inventories fell 0.4%, reversing May's 0.4% gain. On an annual basis, wholesale inventories were up 4.4%.

title: US Goods Trade Deficit Narrows as Exports, Imports Fall
summary: The US goods trade deficit narrowed to $101.5 billion in June 2026 from a 14-month high of $105.9 billion in May, according to preliminary data. Exports fell 1.8% to $204.7 billion, marking a second straight monthly decline and moving further below April's record high, driven by lower shipments of industrial supplies (-4.4%), foods, feeds, and beverages (-3.1%), and capital goods (-1.1%). Imports declined at a faster 2.6% to $306.2 billion, with purchases falling across all major categories, including consumer goods (-3.8%), capital goods (-2.0%), industrial supplies (-1.9%), vehicles (-2.5%), and foods, feeds, and beverages (-2.5%). In the first half of 2026, the cumulative goods trade deficit narrowed to $535.5 billion from $716.6 billion in the same period a year earlier, suggesting trade flows are continuing to normalize following last year's US tariff announcements, although uncertainty surrounding US trade policy remains.

title: TSX Futures Steady After Record High
summary: Futures tracking the S&P/TSX Composite Index were muted on Tuesday after closing at a record high in the prior session, as investors assessed corporate earnings and monitored developments in the Middle East. title: US House Prices Rise More than Expected in May: FHFA
summary: US single-family home prices backed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac increased 0.3% in May 2026, following a 0.1% decrease in April, beating market expectations for a 0.2% increase. Among the nine US census divisions, seasonally adjusted monthly price changes ranged from -0.6% in the Pacific division to +1.4% in the East South Central division. On a yearly basis, home prices rose 2.2% in May, following a 2% increase in April. The 12-month changes ranged from -0.3% in the Pacific division to +4.5% in the Middle Atlantic division.

title: US Home Price Growth Accelerates in May
summary: The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller 20-City Home Price Index rose 1.6% year-over-year in May 2026, accelerating from an upwardly revised 1.2% increase in April and exceeding market expectations of 1.3%. The annual gain was the strongest since August 2025. However, after adjusting for inflation, home prices declined for a 12th consecutive month, as May's 4.2% inflation rate outpaced nominal home price growth by 2.6 percentage points. For a third straight month, Chicago recorded the strongest annual price increase among the 20 cities, up 6.9%, followed by New York (4.2%) and Cleveland (3.1%). Meanwhile, Las Vegas posted the steepest decline (-1.9%), ahead of Seattle (-1.8%), Denver (-1.8%), and Tampa (-1.6%). On a monthly basis, home prices increased 0.9%, easing slightly from gains of 1.0% in April and 1.1% in March but continuing to reflect the seasonal strength typically seen during the spring homebuying season. On a seasonally adjusted basis, prices rose 0.2% from the previous month.

title: Cotton Falls from One-Week High

Following its fifth driest June on record, the country's rainfall deficit narrowed to 16% from nearly 40% at the end of June, as widespread rains in recent weeks helped provide rain-fed irrigation to farmland's, easing fears of a supply shortfall. Meanwhile, lower oil prices weighed on demand, reducing cotton's competitiveness against polyester fibers. However, India's cotton-sown area was still down 4% year-on-year at 9.87 million hectares, reflecting slower planting across several major producing states. In Brazil, growers are expected to reduce cotton planted area by 4% in the 2025/26 season despite record exports in 2024/25, as weaker prices discouraged acreage expansion.

The Federal Reserve is expected to hold its policy rates unchanged tomorrow, but rate futures continued reflect the consensus of a hike this year. title: Japan Food Sales Tax Set at 1% Under Takaichi’s Proposal
summary: Japan plans to temporarily cut its sales tax on food and drinks to 1% for two years, Bloomberg reported. The government chose a low positive rate instead of zero to avoid the costly, time-consuming reprogramming of retailers’ cash registers; a 0% rate would take about a year to implement, while 1% could halve that timeline. To take effect in April 2027, the measure must still be legislated and passed by the Diet (parliament), with draft legislation expected in an extraordinary session in autumn 2026. Policymakers hope the measure will ease household burdens, though economists warned that prices may not fall as much as expected, limiting the benefit for consumers.

The latest escalation worsens Europe’s gas supply outlook as the region races to replenish storage ahead of the winter heating season. title: Heating Oil Moves Back Toward 3-Month High
summary: US heating oil prices rose to around $4.20 per gallon, moving back toward their three-month high, as the resumption of hostilities between Iran and the US revived fears of energy supply disruptions. Iran launched ballistic missiles at US forces in the Middle East, marking an escalation after a pause in fighting although the US Central Command said all missiles were intercepted. The US military also conducted strikes with Saudi forces in Iraq targeting Iran-backed militant groups in response to Iranian-directed drone attacks. In the Strait of Hormuz, Iran rejected Oman’s proposal to split control of shipping routes, insisting the inbound route and part of the outbound route remain under Tehran’s control. Outside the Middle East, Russia’s fuel crisis has started to ease as refineries resumed operations, but the diesel export ban continues to pressure an already tight diesel market. Elsewhere, industry data showed distillate stockpiles fell by 125,000 barrels in the week ending July 24.

title: Gasoline Rises on Renewed US-Iran Hostilities
summary: US gasoline prices rose to around $3.37 per gallon, moving back toward a two-month high, as renewed tensions between Iran and the US revived concerns over energy supply disruptions. Meanwhile, Iran rejected Oman’s proposal to share oversight of shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz, demanding control over the inbound route and a portion of outbound traffic. Outside the region, Russia eased gasoline purchase restrictions in several areas as supply conditions improved, but the extension of its export ban through year-end continued to limit relief for global gasoline availability. Elsewhere, industry data showed gasoline inventories rose by 918,000 barrels in the week ending July 24.

title: Platinum Trades Near Multi-Month Lows
summary: Platinum futures traded around $1,600 an ounce, near late-November lows, pressured by weakness across precious metals amid persistent hostilities in the Middle East. The conflict kept inflation risks in focus and reinforced expectations that interest rates could stay higher for longer, weighing on non-yielding assets such as platinum. Investors now await the Federal Reserve's policy decision, where rates are widely expected to remain unchanged. Still, markets see about a one-third chance of a rate hike this week and roughly an 80% chance of another increase in September. The platinum market was also weighed down by expectations for softer industrial and automotive demand despite the tight supply outlook. The ongoing shift toward electric vehicles, which do not require autocatalysts, has clouded demand prospects even as the platinum market is forecast to post a fourth straight annual supply deficit due to constrained mine supply and declining above-ground inventories.

title: Australia Inflation Rate at 4-Month Low of 3.8%
summary: The annual inflation rate in Australia unexpectedly eased to 3.8% in June 2026 from both May's reading and market expectations of 4.0%, but remained above the central bank's 2–3% target range. It was the softest increase since February, as goods inflation moderated to 3.5% from 4.2%, the lowest in four months, with transport costs rising at the slowest pace in four months (0.1% vs 3.3% in May). Inflation also slowed for health (3.7% vs 3.8%). Meanwhile, price growth accelerated for recreation (3.3% vs 2.4%) and housing (6.8% vs 6.5%), while inflation for food and non-alcoholic beverages remained steady at 3.3%. Services inflation also picked up to 4.0% from 3.7%. Meanwhile, the trimmed mean CPI stood at 3.6% yoy, still the highest since September 2024 but below expectations of 3.7%, while the weighted median CPI rose 3.7%, after a 3.6% increase in May. Monthly, the CPI unexpectedly edged down 0.1%, marking its second consecutive monthly decline and defying expectations of a 0.2% rise.

title: PBoC Maintains Liquidity Support Before Month-End
summary: The People's Bank of China (PBoC) injected CNY 806.5 billion into the banking system through reverse repo operations on Wednesday, July 29, 2026, to maintain ample liquidity at month-end. The central bank supplied CNY 206.5 billion via seven-day reverse repos at an unchanged interest rate of 1.40%, while adding another CNY 600 billion through overnight reverse repos without disclosing the borrowing cost. The move followed the PBoC's announcement last week that it would conduct overnight reverse repo operations from July 29 to 31 and again on August 3, injecting a total of CNY 2.1 trillion through the short-term liquidity tool. The operations reflect the central bank's continued efforts to stabilize money market conditions and ensure sufficient cash in the banking system during a period of typically elevated funding demand at the end of the month.

title: Aussie Dollar Dips on Softer CPI Data
summary: The Australian dollar fell below $0.695, reaching its weakest level in two weeks as softer inflation data dampened expectations of additional interest rate hikes. Meanwhile, the closely watched trimmed mean inflation rate rose 3.6% annually, below expectations of 3.7%, while quarterly core inflation increased 0.8%, also undershooting forecasts. The softer readings also reinforced the view that the central bank is unlikely to resume policy tightening at its August 11 meeting. Still, the central bank's governor recently warned that another rate hike may still be needed to bring inflation back to target.

summary: Wheat futures rose more than 1% to around $6.70 per bushel in late July, recovering further from sharp losses on July 27 as escalating risks to Black Sea grain shipments stoked concerns over tightening global supplies.
