On the demand front, cargo surveyors estimated Malaysia's palm oil exports for July 1–25 increased between 8.1% and 15.9% from the same period in June. Meanwhile, palm oil imports by top buyer India are expected to rise between July and October as tighter edible oil supplies ahead of the festive season lift buying interest. Meanwhile, Indonesia is reportedly seeking a U.S. exemption for palm oil under the new 10% tariff regime to safeguard its export competitiveness. However, gains were tempered by a stronger ringgit and reports that European Union palm oil imports for the 2026/27 marketing year, which began in July, plunged 39% yoy to 0.13 million tonnes.

title: TAIEX Extends Slide, Stays at Over 2-Month Low
summary: The TAIEX, Taiwan's benchmark stock index, slumped 1,397 points, or 3.74%, to 40,206 in Wednesday morning deals, down for the fourth consecutive session and marking its lowest level since May 20, as a global selloff in chipmakers continued to weigh on technology heavyweights. Electronic technology stocks plunged 4.2%, after slumping 5.3% in the previous session, with TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, accounting for more than 40% of the market's total value, falling 2.4% following a 3.0% drop a day earlier. Meanwhile, Delta Electronics and MediaTek plunged 7.6% and 7.5%, respectively. Among the major memory chip suppliers, Nanya Technology Corp. and Winbond Electronics Corp. plunged 9.9% and 9.7%, respectively. However, traders awaited the Fed's interest rate decision later today amid rising oil prices due to the escalating conflict in the Middle East.

title: Singapore Producer Inflation Slows in June
summary: Singapore’s domestic supply price index climbed 30.3% year-on-year in June 2026, slowing from a downwardly revised 34.1% jump in the previous month. The slowdown is largely driven by moderating costs for mineral fuels, lubricants and related materials (46.9% vs 76.7% in May), crude materials (13.0% vs 13.3%), and chemical and chemical products (13.4% vs 21.5%). Meanwhile, price growth increased for machinery and transport equipment (35.1% vs 27.5%) and manufactured goods (5.7% vs 5.4%). On the other hand, prices declined for food and live animals, down 1.9% after a 2.5% drop in the prior month. On a monthly basis, the domestic supply price index fell 2.5% in June, marking its second monthly decline of the year and a steeper decrease than the 2.0% drop recorded in the last month.

title: South Korean Stocks Lead Asia Lower
summary: South Korea’s KOSPI Composite Index tumbled 8% on Wednesday, extending the previous session’s nearly 11% slump and falling to its lowest level since early April as the selloff in semiconductor stocks intensified amid mounting concerns over artificial intelligence spending and elevated valuations. Among individual companies, SK Hynix plunged nearly 13% after the chipmaker reported another record quarterly profit but missed analyst expectations. Technology-heavy benchmark indexes in Japan and China also traded lower, while markets in Australia and Hong Kong outperformed the broader regional trend. On the geopolitical front, the US military said it had successfully intercepted what it described as a surprise Iranian attack targeting US troops stationed across the Middle East, reigniting regional tensions and pushing oil prices higher.

title: Soybean Futures Near 2-Week Low
summary: Soybean futures fell below $12.1 per bushel, approaching a two-week low as expectations of ample global supplies offset support from strong US export demand and deteriorating crop conditions. The USDA lowered its good-to-excellent rating for the nation's soybean crop to 63% from 66% a week earlier, reflecting persistent heat in parts of the Midwest. At the same time, China's Sinograin plans to auction 500,000 metric tons of imported soybeans, its largest sale since January, to free up storage ahead of new US arrivals, reinforcing expectations for continued US export demand. The USDA also reported multiple soybean export sales to China earlier this month, including 340,000 metric tons and 264,000 metric tons, alongside 256,634 metric tons to Mexico. Meanwhile, Brazil is expected to export a record 115.4 million metric tons of soybeans in 2026, according to crushers group Abiove, raising its outlook by 1.1% from a June projection while increasing soy crushing estimates.

title: Corn Holds Near Multi-Week Highs
summary: Corn futures held above $4.5 per bushel, staying near their highest level since late May as geopolitical disruptions raised concerns over global supplies, while persistent dry weather in parts of the US Midwest threatened yields. The USDA said that 63% of the country's corn crop was rated good-to-excellent, down from 67% a week earlier and below market expectations. Meanwhile, continued attacks between Russia and Ukraine raised concerns over Black Sea grain exports, with damage to port infrastructure and shipping routes threatening supplies from one of the world's key exporting regions. Additionally, renewed fighting in the Middle East constrained fertilizer shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and pushed crude oil prices higher. Higher energy prices supported corn by improving the outlook for ethanol demand. The market also remained underpinned by the USDA's latest WASDE report, which cut 2026/27 US ending stocks more than expected while raising export forecasts.

title: Rupiah Stays Fragile Amid BI Leadership Shake-Up
summary: The Indonesian rupiah hovered around IDR 18,090 per U.S. dollar on Wednesday, remaining under strain from policy uncertainty following the sudden exit of Perry Warjiyo as central bank governor. Local reports suggested his departure followed a major dispute with the finance minister over growth strategies, though whether the disagreement directly triggered his exit remains unclear. The president’s spokesperson denied speculation of government pressure. Some economists said a permanent appointment for the new chief is expected within the next two months, with markets likely to stay cautious until the successor is formally named. Bank Indonesia raised rates by a cumulative 100bps since May to shore up the currency and attract foreign inflows. Yet the rupiah has still slipped about 8% this year, extending losses from the past two years. On the global front, the U.S. dollar index steadied ahead of the Fed’s policy decision later today, with markets broadly expecting rates to stay unchanged.

title: Sensex Rises on Tech Strength
summary: India’s BSE Sensex rose about 1.0% to 77,538 on Wednesday, recovering losses from the previous session, as technology stocks led the gains ahead of the US Fed Reserve’s policy decision. The benchmark index was led higher by technology stocks, with NewGen (5.3%), KPIT Tech (4.3%), Coforge (4.2%), Infosys (3.9%), and TCS (2.8%) among the notable gainers. Other strong performers across sectors included SHK (14%), Paradeep (12%), and Firstsource Solutions (6.6%). Sentiment was also supported by renewed foreign buying, with foreign institutional investors (FIIs) turning net buyers of approximately INR 7.55 billion in the previous session. Investors also monitored corporate earnings, with Larsen & Toubro remaining in focus after reaffirming its full-year revenue and margin guidance following a strong quarterly performance. However, gains were capped by higher crude oil prices, as rising geopolitical tensions pushed Brent crude higher, posing a potential risk to India as a major oil importer.

title: FX Updates: South Korean Won Appreciates by 0.56%
summary: Top currency gainers are South Korean Won (0.56%), Norwegian Krone (0.26%), Japanese Yen (0.26%), Euro (0.13%) and British Pound (0.08%). Biggest losers are Australian Dollar (-0.29%) and Dollar Index (-0.15%).

title: NZX 50 Rally Persists, Ends at Fresh Record High
summary: New Zealand's stocks rose 115 points, or 0.8%, to close at a record high of 13,977 on Wednesday, marking their third consecutive record close, with almost all sectors trading in the green. The gains were mainly driven by materials, healthcare, consumer staples, and communication services. Traders maintained momentum as they braced for the upcoming earnings season next month, though oil prices rebounded amid renewed escalation of the conflict in the Middle East and the global tech selloff. However, traders remained cautious ahead of the Fed's interest rate decision later today. The top performer was AFT Pharmaceuticals (7.6%) after the company said its portfolio of projects opened the business up to multi-billion-dollar market opportunities. Other notable gainers were Ebos Group (4.6%), Fisher & Paykel Healthcare (2.5%), Chorus (2.5%), Delegat Group (1.7%), A2 Milk (1.4%), Mercury NZ (1.2%), Auckland International Airport (0.9%), and Infratil (0.9%).

title: Swedish Economic Activity Shrinks 0.2% in June
summary: The Swedish economy shrank 0.2% month on month in June 2026, reversing a 0.9% expansion in the previous month and marking the first contraction in four months. "The Swedish economy contracted somewhat in June following three months of continuous growth. Those stronger figures in the preceding months led to levels of economic activity for both June and the second quarter as a whole that were noticeably above the levels seen in the corresponding periods of the preceding year," said Mattias Kain Wyatt, economist at Statistics Sweden. On a yearly basis, GDP expanded 2.4% in June, easing from a downwardly revised 3.8% expansion in May.

title: Sweden GDP Growth Strongest in Over 2 Years
summary: The Swedish economy expanded 1.4% quarter-on-quarter in the three months to June 2026, sharply rebounding from a 0.2% contraction in the previous period and exceeding market expectations of a 0.7% growth, according to preliminary estimates. It marked the sharpest quarterly expansion since the first quarter of 2024, reflecting stronger economic activity in the earlier months of the quarter despite a modest decline in June. Mattias Kain Wyatt of Statistics Sweden said June's pullback followed three consecutive months of growth and that overall economic activity remained well above year-earlier levels. On an annual basis, GDP grew 2.8%, accelerating from 2.0% in the previous quarter, and marking the fastest annual expansion since the fourth quarter of 2024.

title: European Stocks Poised for Cautious Open
summary: European equity markets were set to open modestly lower on Wednesday as investors remained cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s policy decision, while renewed hostilities in the Middle East added to geopolitical uncertainty. A global selloff in semiconductor stocks, fueled by growing concerns over heavy artificial intelligence spending and stretched valuations, also continued to weigh on market sentiment. In Europe, investors are looking ahead to the Bank of England’s policy decision and GDP data from across the region due on Thursday. On the corporate front, banking giants UBS Group and Standard Chartered announced fresh share buyback programs after reporting stronger-than-expected earnings. Markets will also monitor earnings reports from L’Oreal, Hermes, Airbus, AON, and Deutsche Bank, among others. In premarket trading, Euro Stoxx 50 futures slipped 0.2%, while Stoxx 600 futures edged down 0.1%.

title: Norway Retail Sales Growth Hits Near 2-Year High
summary: Retail sales in Norway grew 1.8% month over month in June 2026, rebounding from an upwardly revised 2.4% drop in May, which was the steepest decline since June 2024. It was the fastest increase in retail sales since May 2024, driven by a rebound in sales at non-specialized stores (1.6% vs -2.1% in May), food, beverages, and tobacco stores (1.8% vs -1.6%), ICT equipment stores (0.1% vs -5.3%), other household equipment stores (1.7% vs -1.3%), cultural and recreational goods stores (3.8% vs -6.9%), while sales through non-store retailing rose at a much faster pace (1.9% vs 0.1%). Additionally, sales fell at a slower pace for automotive fuel (-3.0% vs -3.4%) and other goods (-0.7% vs -2.6%). On an annual basis, retail sales fell by 0.3%, after a downwardly revised 2.3% drop in May.

title: German Import Prices Ease from 2-1/2-Year High
summary: Germany’s import prices rose 6.1% yoy in June 2026, easing from May’s 6.8%, which had marked the strongest gain since December 2022. The latest reading was slightly above market expectations of 6.0%, extending the current streak of annual gains to four months. Energy prices remained the main driver, though their pace slowed (23.9% vs 37.2% in May), with notable rises in electricity (70.8%), petroleum (36.0%), crude oil (32.1%), hard coal (12.1%), and natural gas (8.3%). Cost of intermediate goods accelerated (10.3% vs 10.1%), due to higher prices of non-ferrous metals and semi-finished products (27.5%), including precious metals (34.5%) and copper (30.3%). Capital goods inflation also strengthened (2.9% vs 2.2%). By contrast, consumer goods prices continued to fall (-0.8% vs -1.3%), as non-durable goods dropped 1.2% while durable goods rose 0.7%. Monthly, import prices slipped 0.7%, reversing May’s 0.7% rise and signaling the first monthly drop since December, in line with estimates.

title: UK Gas Prices Advance
summary: UK natural gas prices rose above 143 pence per therm on Wednesday after a two-day decline, as renewed hostilities in the Middle East heightened concerns over prolonged supply disruptions. The US military said on Tuesday it had intercepted multiple missiles launched by Iran, ending a days-long lull in fighting between the two sides. Both nations had largely held fire over the weekend following nearly two weeks of nightly US strikes on Iran and repeated attacks by Tehran targeting Washington's allies across the Gulf. The latest escalation worsens Europe’s gas supply outlook as the region races to replenish storage ahead of the winter. Supply concerns were further exacerbated by reports that QatarEnergy, one of the world's largest LNG exporters, has extended its force majeure for European buyers until at least the end of September.

title: Fed to Keep Rates Steady, but Odds of a Hike Persist
summary: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to leave the federal funds rate unchanged at 3.50%–3.75% for a fifth consecutive meeting in July 2026. However, the decision remains a close call, with markets assigning nearly a 30% probability to a rate hike. Policymakers continue to navigate heightened uncertainty driven by renewed tensions between the US and Iran and elevated oil prices, even as inflation has come in softer than expected and the labor market has remained resilient. US inflation eased to 3.5% in June, marking its first decline in five months. Investors will closely monitor both the voting split which has highlighted growing divisions within the Federal Reserve, and Chair Warsh's second press conference for clues about the likelihood of a rate hike in September. Markets are currently pricing in roughly a 77% probability of an increase at that meeting. Chair Warsh has repeatedly emphasized that restoring price stability remains the Federal Reserve's foremost priority.

title: Uzbekistan Holds Benchmark Rate at 14%
summary: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan left its key policy rate unchanged at 14% during its July 2026 meeting, maintaining a tight monetary stance to bring inflation to its 5% target amid strong domestic demand and persistent price pressures. Annual inflation accelerated to 6.4% in June, driven mainly by higher regulated energy tariffs and the liberalization of coal prices, while core inflation held steady at 5.7%. The central bank kept its 2026 inflation forecast unchanged at 6.5%, citing strong domestic demand, second-round effects of tariff adjustments, and external uncertainties. Meanwhile, the economy remained resilient, with GDP expanding 8.5% in the first half of the year, supported by robust consumer activity, investment demand, and foreign direct investment inflows. The central bank reiterated that current monetary conditions remain sufficiently tight to curb inflationary pressures and inflation expectations while continuing to shape monetary conditions to ensure price stability.

title: TAIEX Closes at Over-2-Month Low on Tech Weakness
summary: The TAIEX, Taiwan's benchmark stock index, plunged 1,564 points, or 3.8%, to close at 40,039 on Wednesday, down for the fourth consecutive session and marking its lowest level since May 20, as a global selloff in chipmakers continued to weigh on technology heavyweights. Growing concerns over revenue amid heavy AI investments weighed on sentiment after the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index shed 4.5% overnight. The broader index tracked losses in US stock futures ahead of the Fed's monetary policy decision amid rising oil prices due to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. Electronic technology stocks slumped 4.5%, after falling 5.3% in the previous session, with TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, accounting for more than 40% of the market's total value, declining 2.2% following a 3.0% drop a day earlier. Meanwhile, ASE Technology Holding, Delta Electronics, and MediaTek slumped 9.9%, 7.9%, and 7.5%, respectively.

title: ASX 200 Climbs to Highest Since March on Inflation Relief
summary: Australia's ASX 200 jumped 91 points, or 1.0%, to end at 9,039 on Wednesday, extending gains for a third session and reaching its highest level since early March. Softer CPI data eased pressure on the Reserve Bank after three hikes earlier this year. However, gains were limited by weaker U.S. stock futures as oil prices surged following Iran's attack on U.S. forces. Meanwhile, investors cautiously awaited the Fed's interest rate decision and Chairman Kevin Warsh's briefing later in the day. Nearly all sectors advanced, led by healthcare, retail, consumer services, and consumer non-durables. Rio Tinto rallied 3.7% on its strongest first-half earnings in four years and its largest interim dividend since 2022. CSL surged 7.2% after announcing trials of a new immunoglobulin manufacturing process. Woodside Energy rose 1.4% as Q2 revenue jumped 28% and full-year guidance was narrowed. In contrast, three of the four major banks were subdued, with only ANZ Group managing a gain, rising 1.4%.

title: Stocks in United Kingdom Hit All-time High
summary: GB100 increased to an all-time high of 10949.00 Index Points. Over the past 4 weeks, United Kingdom Stock Market Index (GB100) gained 4.43%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 19.84%.

title: India 10Y Yield Rises Ahead of Fed
summary: The yield on India’s 10-year G-Sec rose to around 6.79%, snapping three consecutive sessions of losses as investors turned cautious ahead of the conclusion of the Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting and rising oil prices weighed on sentiment. Markets assigned a 65% probability to the Fed holding interest rates steady while fully pricing in a 25-basis-point hike in September, with traders closely watching Chair Kevin Warsh's guidance on the policy outlook. Meanwhile, Brent crude climbed 4.7% to around $87.68 per barrel after US and Saudi forces launched strikes on Iran-backed groups in Iraq, reviving concerns over the Middle East conflict and its inflationary impact. Additional upward pressure came from the 10-year US Treasury yield, which edged up to 4.61%, while investors continued to expect the Reserve Bank of India to keep its repo rate unchanged at 5.25% at next week's policy meeting.

title: FTSE 100 Trades At Record-High
summary: The FTSE 100 climbed to near-record highs above 10,900 on Wednesday, supported by strong corporate earnings from several heavyweight constituents. Rio Tinto gained around 1.8% after reporting a sharp rise in second-quarter profit and outlining plans to further reduce costs and strengthen cash generation. Standard Chartered advanced nearly 3% as the bank posted better-than-expected quarterly earnings and announced a new share buyback. Reckitt was among the top performers, surging about 7% after quarterly sales exceeded forecasts, following similarly upbeat results from Unilever. Glencore also rose more than 4% after forecasting first-half marketing earnings of roughly $3.3 billion. Oil majors BP and Shell added over 1% as Brent crude rebounded amid renewed geopolitical tensions. Meanwhile, Aberdeen Group fell more than 5.5% on weaker first-half fund flows, while St James’s Place slipped 0.5% despite reporting stronger-than-expected assets under management and continued client inflows.

title: DAX 40 at Three-Week High as Fed Decision Looms
summary: Frankfurt's DAX 40 rose 0.3% to around 25,520 on Wednesday, its highest level since July 6, as investors awaited the US Federal Reserve's policy decision due after the European market close while digesting fresh earnings and higher oil prices. Semiconductor stocks remained under pressure, with Infineon falling another 1% after Tuesday's 6% drop, amid concerns over stretched valuations, stronger Chinese competition, and rising investment needs. Among individual movers, Deutsche Bank jumped 4% after reporting stronger-than-expected second-quarter earnings, driven by record profits in its investment banking division. RWE gained more than 3% following better-than-expected first-half results, while BASF advanced 2% after announcing a new share buyback program. Meanwhile, oil prices surged more than 3%, supported by renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and a larger-than-expected drawdown in US crude inventories, adding to concerns over inflationary pressures in Europe.

title: European Stocks Cautious
summary: European stocks traded cautiously on Wednesday, with the STOXX 50 fluctuating around the flatline and the STOXX 600 edging 0.1% higher, as investors continued to assess a fresh batch of corporate earnings while as ?a rout in chip stocks deepened and oil prices increased, following another setback in the Middle East. LVMH extended Tuesday's gains, rising 3.2% after reporting broadly in-line sales growth. Eni surged nearly 4% after raising its 2026 production forecast. Deutsche Bank advanced 4.3% after posting a 10% increase in profit, defying expectations for a decline, while Porsche gained 1.2% after reporting a 34% rise in first-half operating profit. On the downside, ASML Holding fell 2.5%, Hermes was down 2.8% as its results failed to impress investors. Danone lost 3% after second-quarter sales growth was driven by higher prices rather than stronger volumes. Investors also awaited earnings from L'Oréal (-0.9%), Airbus (-0.6%), and Intesa Sanpaolo (+0.6%) later in the day.

title: UK Gilt Yields Rise on Oil-Driven Inflation Concerns
summary: The UK 10-year gilt yield climbed to 4.97% on Wednesday, rebounding from two-week lows as renewed military exchanges between the US and Iran drove oil prices higher, reviving inflation concerns. Investors also remained cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy decision later in the day and the Bank of England's meeting on Thursday, both of which are expected to provide further guidance on the outlook for interest rates. The Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep rates unchanged, although markets still assign roughly a 30% chance of a 25-basis-point hike. In the UK, the Bank of England is also expected to leave its Bank Rate at 3.75%, with investors closely watching the vote split for clues on the future policy path. Recent data showed UK inflation slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6% in June, below the BoE's forecast. However, businesses and government officials have warned that the recent spike in energy prices could lift inflation again in the coming months.

title: Pound Steadies Near One-Month Low Ahead of Fed and BoE Decisions
summary: The British pound traded around $1.33 on Wednesday, little changed from the previous session and hovering near its weakest level in almost a month, as investors awaited policy decisions from the US Federal Reserve later in the day and the Bank of England on Thursday. The Fed is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged, though markets still price in roughly a 30% chance of a 25-basis-point hike. In the UK, the BoE is also expected to keep its Bank Rate at 3.75%, with investors focusing on the vote split for signals on the future policy path. Recent data showed UK inflation slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6% in June, below the BoE's forecast, supporting expectations of a pause. However, concerns persist that the recent surge in energy prices could rekindle inflationary pressures in the months ahead as higher costs feed through to households and businesses.

title: Energy Commodities Updates: Brent Crude Oil Gains by 3.75%
summary: Top commodity gainers are Brent Crude Oil (3.75%), Crude Oil WTI (3.57%) and Heating Oil (2.36%). Biggest loser is Natural gas (-0.65%).

title: Metals Commodities Updates: Silver Gains by 1.65%
summary: Top commodity gainers are Silver (1.65%) and Gold (0.38%). Biggest loser is Platinum (-0.59%).

title: Euro Holds Near One-Month Low Ahead of Fed Decision
summary: The euro remained under pressure below the $1.14 mark, hovering near its weakest level in a month as renewed US-Iran hostilities lifted oil prices and reignited inflation concerns. Investors also remained cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision later in the day, with the central bank widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged, although markets still assign roughly a one-third chance of a 25-basis-point hike. In the euro area, money markets are pricing in nearly two 25-basis-point ECB rate hikes by March 2027. ECB policymaker Peter Kazimir said at least one more increase will likely be needed to bring inflation under control, adding that a weaker economic outlook could warrant even more tightening than markets currently expect. Meanwhile, Chief Economist Philip Lane said the current inflation shock remains moderate, supporting further policy tightening. Investors now await euro area inflation data later this week for fresh clues on the ECB's policy path.

title: Agricultural Commodities Updates: Palm Oil Rises by 0.78%
summary: Top commodity gainers are Palm Oil (0.78%), Oat (0.70%) and Canola (0.50%). Biggest loser is Soybeans (-0.68%).

title: Bund Yield Rises as Oil Rally Revives Inflation Concerns
summary: Germany's 10-year Bund yield climbed to 3.12%, rebounding from two-week lows as renewed military exchanges between the US and Iran lifted oil prices and renewed inflation concerns. Investors also remained cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision later in the day, with the central bank widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged, although markets continue to price in roughly a one-third chance of a 25 bp hike. In the euro area, money markets are pricing in nearly two ECB rate hikes by March 2027. ECB Governing Council member Peter Kazimir said at least one more rate increase will likely be needed to bring inflation under control, adding that a weaker economic outlook could justify even more tightening than markets currently expect. Chief Economist Philip Lane said the current inflation shock remains moderate, reinforcing the case for further policy tightening. Investors now await euro area inflation data later this week for fresh signals on the ECB's policy outlook.

title: Austria Manufacturing Sector Remains in Expansion
summary: The UniCredit Bank Austria Manufacturing PMI rose to 51.5 in July 2026, picking up from a four-month low of 50.9 in the previous month. It remained above the 50 threshold for a fifth consecutive month, as output expanded at its fastest pace since May 2022. Meanwhile, new orders declined at the slowest pace since January, though export orders continued to weaken amid challenging external market conditions. On the price front, input cost inflation eased to a five-month low but remained elevated relative to its long-run average. Output price inflation also moderated from May's recent peak. Looking ahead, Austrian manufacturers grew more optimistic about the year-ahead outlook. Business confidence rebounded sharply from a one-and-a-half-year low in June to its highest level since just before the outbreak of the Middle East conflict in February, reflecting expectations of stronger demand and improved economic conditions.

title: Italy Industrial Sales Rise 0.6% MoM in May
summary: Italy’s industrial turnover increased 0.6% month-on-month in May 2026, after a revised 0.2% fall in the previous month. Foreign sales rebounded (1.6% vs -0.8% in April), while domestic sales rose at a softer pace (0.1% vs 0.2%). On a yearly basis, industrial turnover, adjusted for calendar effects, grew 5.3%, accelerating from a revised 2.7% gain in April, driven by higher sales in both the domestic (4.7% vs 2.8%) and foreign markets (6.6% vs 2.4%). By industrial group, the energy sector continued to post the strongest growth (28.6%), followed by capital goods (6.6%) and intermediate goods (6.1%), while consumer goods sales decreased (-1.4%). Meanwhile, turnover in the services sector edged up 0.2% month-on-month after remaining unchanged in April, supported by increases in professional, scientific, and technical activities (2.0% vs 1.6%), real estate activity (1.8% vs 0.4%), and accommodation and food service activities (1.1% vs 0.8%).

title: National Bank of Georgia Holds Key Rate Steady
summary: The National Bank of Georgia left its key policy rate unchanged at 8.25% at its July 2026 meeting, maintaining a cautious stance amid tensions in the Middle East. Headline inflation edged up to 5.8% in June from 5.7%, driven by higher energy prices linked to the regional conflict. Policymakers noted the increase was broadly in line with expectations for the second quarter, while emphasizing that second-round inflationary effects remain a key concern. Meanwhile, economic activity accelerated to 9.0% year-on-year in the first quarter from 6.7% in the previous quarter, supported by strong performance in service sectors, with the negative impact of the conflict remaining limited. The central bank continues to forecast economic growth of 6.5% in 2026 and revised its average inflation projection up to 5.2% from 4.9%, beginning to ease in the second half of the year and gradually converge to target over the medium term. Future decisions will depend on inflation risks and second-round effects.

title: Swiss Investor Confidence Turns Positive in July
summary: Swiss investor sentiment improved to 10.0 in July 2026 from -25.0 in June, returning to positive territory for the first time since the outbreak of the Middle East conflict in February, according to the UBS & CFA Society Switzerland survey. The expectations index rose sharply to +9.5 from +2.8 in the previous month, signaling stronger optimism about the economic outlook. Meanwhile, the current conditions gauge edged up to +6.7 in July from +2.4 in June, indicating a further improvement in assessments of the present economic environment. UBS also noted that the share of analysts expecting higher oil prices reached its highest level in twelve months, leaving expectations evenly split between rising and falling oil prices.

title: Hermes International Stock Price Hits 7-week Low
summary: Hermes International shares decreased to 1564.00 EUR, the lowest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Hermes International lost 1.78%, and in the last 12 months, it decreased 30.86%.

title: ECB Wage Tracker Points to Slower Pay Growth Despite Inflation Risks
summary: The ECB's wage tracker, which monitors pay agreements negotiated through the first week of July, indicates negotiated wages are set to rise 2.3% in 2026 and 2.7% in the first quarter of 2027, down from 3% growth in 2025. The ECB described the outlook as "stable," suggesting wage pressures are easing despite the recent pickup in inflation driven by the Middle East conflict. ECB policymakers view wage settlements as a key gauge of whether higher energy prices could trigger more persistent inflation above the central bank's 2% target. So far, however, there is little evidence of a wage-price spiral, with wage growth showing no signs of reaccelerating. Even so, investors continue to expect the ECB to deliver a second interest rate hike since the conflict began when policymakers meet in September, reflecting concerns that elevated energy costs could keep inflationary pressures alive.

title: Bulgaria Tourist Arrivals Down 0.2% in June
summary: Tourist arrivals in Bulgaria fell by 0.2% year-on-year to 1,424.1 thousand in June 2026, reversing a 2.4% increase in the previous month. Visits for holiday and recreation accounted for the largest share of total arrivals at 52.3%, followed by visits for other purposes at 39.7% and business and professional visits at 8.0%. Visitors from European Union countries totaled 812.8 thousand, representing 57.1% of all arrivals, with Romania (30.3%) remaining the leading source of visits. Meanwhile, tourists from other European countries accounted for 36.9%, or 525.6 thousand arrivals, led by Turkey, which represented 46.1% or 242.2 thousand of these visits. Transit travelers passing through Bulgaria reached 420.7 thousand during the month, accounting for 29.5% of all visits by foreign citizens.

title: UK Consumer Credit Rises More than Expected
summary: Net borrowing of consumer credit by individuals in the UK slightly increased to £1.807 billion in June 2026 from £1.7 billion in May, and beating market forecasts of £1.7 billion. This was in line with the previous 6-month average of £1.8 billion. Within this, net borrowing through credit cards was £0.9 billion in June, up from £0.6 billion in May. Net borrowing through other forms of consumer credit, such as car dealership finance and personal loans, decreased to £0.9 billion in June, from £1.1 billion in May. The annual growth rate for all consumer credit increased slightly to 9.1% in June, the most since July 2018, from 9.0% in May. Over the same period, the annual growth rate for credit card borrowing increased to 12.5% from 12.2%, while for other forms of consumer credit it remained unchanged at 7.6%.

title: UK Mortgage Approvals Rise in June Despite Higher Borrowing Costs
summary: Net mortgage approvals for house purchases in the UK, a key indicator of future borrowing, rose to 58,200 in June 2026 from a revised 56,600 in May, exceeding market expectations of 57,100. Despite the increase, approvals remained near two-year lows and below the previous six-month average of around 61,400, reflecting the impact of elevated borrowing costs. Approvals for remortgaging with a different lender also edged higher to 34,200 from 33,800. Meanwhile, the effective interest rate on newly drawn mortgages climbed to 4.35% in June from 4.22% in May, its highest level in more than a year. The average rate on the outstanding stock of mortgages also increased, reaching a record high of 3.96%.

title: UK Mortgage Borrowing Jumps Well Above Expectations in June
summary: Net mortgage borrowing by UK households surged to £7.7 billion in June 2026 from £3.3 billion in May, far exceeding market expectations of £3.95 billion and the previous six-month average of £4.9 billion, despite rising borrowing costs. The annual growth rate of net mortgage lending also edged up to 3.6% from 3.5%. Gross mortgage lending rose slightly to £27.4 billion from £27.2 billion, remaining above the six-month average of £26.0 billion. Meanwhile, repayments fell to £21.3 billion from £22.7 billion, although they continued to exceed the recent six-month average of £20.4 billion. Meanwhile, the effective interest rate on newly drawn mortgages climbed to 4.35% in June from 4.22% in May, its highest level in more than a year. The average rate on the outstanding stock of mortgages also increased, reaching a record high of 3.96%.

title: FX Updates: Australian Dollar Drops by 0.46%
summary: Top currency losers are Australian Dollar (-0.46%) and Dollar Index (-0.21%). Gains are led by Japanese Yen (0.15%), British Pound (0.12%) and Euro (0.08%).

title: Belgium GDP Flat in Q2 of 2026
summary: Belgium's economy was flat in the second quarter of 2026, according to the flash estimate, following a 0.2% expansion in the previous quarter. Initially, the slowdown reflected weaker activity in the goods-producing sectors, with industrial output contracting 0.8% and construction declining 0.5%. In contrast, the services sector continued to provide modest support to the economy, expanding by 0.2%. On an annual basis, GDP grew by 0.5% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, marking the weakest annual expansion since first quarter of 2021 and easing slightly from a 0.8% growth recorded in the previous quarter.

title: Croatia Industrial Output Rises to 7-Month High
summary: Industrial production in Croatia rose 4.3% year-on-year in June 2026, rebounding from a 1.1% decline in May and marking the strongest growth since November 2025. Production accelerated for intermediate goods (14.8% vs 0.4% in May), while declines eased for capital goods (-7.3% vs -11.3%) and consumer non-durables (-1.6% vs -2.8%). Meanwhile, energy production growth slowed (1.2% vs 4.6%), and consumer durables declined further (-13.8% vs -11.2%). By sector, manufacturing output recovered 4.0% after falling 2.5% in May, driven by stronger production of food (6.2% vs 0.7%), basic metals (9.3% vs 5.6%), electrical equipment (94.5% vs 13.6%), and motor vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers (14.4% vs 3.8%). In contrast, mining and quarrying declined further (-6.5% vs -5.1%), while electricity, gas, steam, and air conditioning contracted (-0.7% vs 0.9%). On a seasonally adjusted monthly basis, industrial activity climbed 5.3% after a 1.9% decline in May.

title: Hermes International Stock Price Hits 3-1/2-year Low
summary: Hermes International shares decreased to 1525.00 EUR, the lowest since January 2023. Over the past 4 weeks, Hermes International lost 3.19%, and in the last 12 months, it decreased 31.85%.

title: Greece Jobless Rate Rises to 8.0%
summary: The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate in Greece rose to 8.0% in June 2026, following a downwardly revised 7.8% growth in the previous month. The number of unemployed individuals increased by 12.4 thousand month-on-month to 381.8 thousand but decreased by 58.3 thousand individuals in the same month last year. Unemployment remained significantly higher among women than men, with rates of 10.4% for women and 6.0% for men. Meanwhile, the number of people outside the labour force, those under 75 who are neither employed nor actively seeking employment, fell by 33.0 thousand a month earlier and declined 37.0 thousand year-on-year. The total number of employed persons grew by 16.4 thousand from the prior month to 4,389.2 thousand.

title: European Stocks Slip as Tech Weighs Ahead of Fed Decision
summary: European equities traded lower in choppy session on Wednesday, weighed down by technology stocks ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy decision later in the day, upcoming earnings from major US tech companies, and ongoing tensions in the Middle East. The STOXX 50 fell 0.5%, while the broader STOXX 600 lost 0.3%. Tech stocks led the declines, with ASM International dropping more than 5% despite an upbeat outlook. Sentiment was also hurt after SK Hynix's record quarterly results failed to meet lofty expectations, raising concerns over AI spending. Energy stocks outperformed as oil prices rebounded on renewed Middle East tensions. Among individual movers, Kering surged 12% after Gucci's sales beat expectations, Sopra Steria jumped 13% on raised guidance, Glencore gained 3% after stronger copper output, while UBS and Deutsche Bank rose on solid earnings. Aberdeen fell 5% after reporting larger-than-expected first-half fund outflows.

title: DAX Reverses Lower as Tech Weakness Weighs
summary: Frankfurt's DAX 40 erased early gains to trade 0.3% lower at around 25,380 on Wednesday, as technology stocks weakened and escalating Middle East tensions kept investors cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy decision later in the day. Semiconductor shares remained under pressure, with Infineon slipping 0.3% after Tuesday's 6% plunge. Sentiment was dented by disappointing market reaction to SK Hynix's results, raising fresh concerns over AI-related spending, while investors also awaited earnings from major US tech companies after the market close. Meanwhile, oil prices jumped more than 3% following renewed military strikes involving the US, Saudi Arabia, and Iran, fueling concerns over inflation. Among corporate movers, Deutsche Bank surged 4% after stronger-than-expected second-quarter earnings, RWE gained over 2% on upbeat first-half results, and BASF rose 2.9% after announcing a new share buyback program.

title: Ireland Economy Expands 3.9% in Q2
summary: Ireland’s economy expanded 3.9% quarter-on-quarter in the second quarter of 2026, rebounding from a 7.0% contraction in the previous quarter and ending two consecutive quarters of decline, according to preliminary estimates. This marked the strongest growth since Q1 2025, driven mainly by an increase in the multinational-dominated information and communication sector. On an annual basis, GDP fell 1.6% in Q2, easing from a 13% decline in the previous quarter and marking the third consecutive quarter of contraction after five straight quarters of growth.

title: Cyprus Wage Growth Weakest Since 2021
summary: Average gross monthly earnings of employees in Cyprus eased by 3.7% year-on-year to EUR 2,601 in the first quarter of 2026, following a 4.4% increase in the previous quarter. This marked the weakest wage growth since the third quarter of 2021. Wages for men rose by 3.3% to EUR 2,776 from EUR 2,687in Q1 2025. Meanwhile, wages for women increased by 4.2% to EUR 2,378, compared with EUR 2,282. On a seasonally adjusted quarterly basis, average gross monthly earnings rose by 0.8% to EUR 2,652.

title: Latvia Retail Sales Growth Accelerates
summary: Retail sales in Latvia increased 4.8% year-on-year in June 2026, accelerating from an upwardly revised 3.6% gain in May. Growth strengthened in both food sales (4.6% vs 2.9%) and non-food sales (5.9% vs 5.5%). Within the non-food segment, sales rose further in non-specialized stores (2.2% vs 1.9%) and across several specialized retailers, including electrical household appliances (9.6% vs 5.7%), construction materials and sanitary equipment (11.8% vs 9.0%), cultural and sporting goods (9.0% vs 4.4%), and clothing, footwear, and leather goods (6.4% vs 0.3%). Meanwhile, mail-order and online sales accelerated sharply to 18.6% from 12.3%. Sales of automotive fuel rebounded 2.4% after a 2.1% decline in May. On a monthly basis, retail sales rose 0.6%, quickening from an upwardly revised 0.1% increase in the previous month.

title: Portugal Unemployment Holds at 24-Year Low in June
summary: Portugal's unemployment rate held steady at 5.6% in June 2026, matching its lowest level since early 2002. The gender gap persisted, with unemployment at 6.3% for women compared with a record-low 4.9% for men. The adult unemployment rate remained unchanged at 4.6%, while youth unemployment stood at 18.9%. The number of unemployed edged up by 900 to 316,600, while employment declined by 13,700 to 5.35 million. As a result, the employment rate slipped to 66.2% from 66.5%, and the labor force participation rate eased to 70.2% from 70.4%. Meanwhile, the broader labor underutilization rate, which includes unemployed, underemployed, and marginally attached workers, fell slightly to 9.3% from 9.4%.

title: Rice Eases from 18-Month High
summary: Rice prices eased to around $13.7 per hundredweight, retreating from the 18-month high of $14.3 reached on July 22 as traders reassess the balance between weather risks and ample global supplies. Earlier gains were driven by concerns that El Niño and below-normal monsoon rainfall could reduce rice production across major Asian growers, particularly India, Vietnam and the Philippines. Although these risks remain, conditions in India have improved after a revival in monsoon rains accelerated rice planting and significantly narrowed the earlier sowing deficit. In addition, India's rice exports rose 5% in the first half of 2026, supported by strong non-basmati shipments and abundant domestic supplies, helping keep global markets well supplied. However, prices remain relatively elevated because weather uncertainty has not disappeared. Dry conditions could still affect yields later in the season, while the USDA projects tighter US rice supplies and lower ending stocks.

title: Sugar Remains Subdued as Global Supply Outlook Weighs
summary: Sugar prices have been fluctuating below 15 cents per pound, remaining more than 10% lower than a year ago, as expectations of abundant global supplies continue to outweigh emerging production risks. The main bearish factor is India, where improved monsoon rains have boosted prospects for a larger sugar crop, while government measures to limit stock holdings aim to ensure adequate domestic availability. Lower crude oil prices have also pressured sugar, as weaker ethanol prices encourage mills, particularly in Brazil, to divert more sugarcane toward sugar production rather than ethanol, increasing supply. However, downside pressure has been partly offset by forecasts of a global sugar deficit in 2026/27, reflecting lower output in Brazil and Thailand and the potential impact of a strengthening El Niño on key producing regions. Meanwhile, the USDA revised US sugar stocks lower following data corrections and projects tighter domestic supplies.
